## Representative Change Workflow

To add or modify a gameplay modifier or runtime command:

0. **For a drop lever, model the change first (before step 1):**
   - A change to `droprate`, `dungeonkey`, the relic pre-roll or a drop slider in `KEYS` is first expressed against `hs_game_sdk.drop_roll_model` in the hub's `tests/test_drop_roll_model.py`: a baseline test for the vanilla roll and a target test for the new lever, with the lever written as an input transform in the test, not in the SDK. Update the transform and `LeverParityTests` together with the plugin, and run `py -3 -m unittest tests.test_drop_roll_model -v` from the hub root.
   - The model settles the arithmetic (what a chance below 1 does, whether a multiplier squares, whether a base is read at all) without a launch. It cannot settle whether a hook attaches, frame timing, value kinds or how a rate feels in play; those still need the live steps below. The mechanism and its limits: `docs/models/drop-roll-spec.md`; the workflow: `docs/agents/static-model-workflow.md`.
1. **Update Plugin Implementation (`plugin/ModuleMain.cpp`):**
   - Add or modify the command parser inside `DoCommand(const std::string& line)`.
   - Implement the corresponding hook or memory override. Ensure hot-path diagnostic counters are wrapped in `#ifndef FORGEPACT_RELEASE` (`BP_DIAG_INCREMENT`).
   - If introducing a functional hook, ensure it is installed lazily only when non-vanilla values are requested (preserving zero-overhead all-off baseline).
2. **Compile Native Plugin (`plugin_build/build.bat`):**
   - Build the release DLL:
     ```cmd
     plugin_build\build.bat release
     ```
   - Copy the output binary to the shipped staging directory:
     ```powershell
     Copy-Item plugin_build\BloodPactPlugin_ship.dll modfiles_shipped\BloodPactPlugin.dll
     ```
3. **Update Panel UI & Command Builder (`src/forgepact.py`):**
   - If adding a new setting, define its metadata in `SPAWNERS`, `KEYS`, `STATS`, or `PERCENT_STATS`.
   - Update `build_cmds(cfg)` and any specialized command generators (e.g. `build_key_cmds`).
   - Update the panel's frontend under `panel/src/` (since the UI port, `src/forgepact.py` holds no page): the tab's `.svelte` file for static markup, `panel.js` for rows drawn from `ST` and for handlers.
   - A new slider row in one of those tables gets its on/off switch from `row()` in `panel/src/panel.js`, with no extra markup; add its id to `SLIDER_SWITCH_IDS` in `src/forgepact.py` (a new top-level slider needs its switch written into its `.svelte` file by hand, like `#rarity_rare`'s). Decide too whether it belongs in `enabledControls()` (`panel/src/enabled-mods.js`) and add the case to `enabled-mods.test.js`.
   - A new control of any kind is not in the recorded behaviour oracle. Never re-record `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle.json`: it is the legacy page's recording and the only proof the port kept every old control's behaviour. The derivation starts from the legacy file's `controls` list, so a control the legacy page never had is covered only once `panel/tests/oracle-derive.mjs` generates steps for it: extend the derivation's contract, re-run `npm run oracle:derive` in `panel/`, and commit the regenerated `behaviour-oracle-derived.json` with the change - never hand-edit either JSON file. For a new boolean mod that is one entry in `NATIVE_BOOLEANS` (`panel/tests/oracle-derive.mjs`: its key, tab, Mods sub-tab and plugin verb), which derives on / off / on / Turn off with literal expectations after every other step (Far scenery sleep, 2026-09-28, was the first); update the step counts in `oracle-derive.test.js` with it. A new switched slider is one entry in `NATIVE_SLIDERS` (its section, key, tab, range and the `cmd.txt` line at each end), which derives a legacy slider's eight steps with literal expectations at both ends, after the native booleans (Skill Haste and All Skills, #114, were the first; Mining Ore Extra Rolls, #36, is appended after them, on the Loot tab, and a tab step is derived each time the tab changes); its range and its switch both go into `controls`, since no recording lists the range. A new select is one entry in `NATIVE_SELECTS` (its key, tab, Mods sub-tab, the value it is raised to and the plugin verb), which derives raised / off / raised / Turn off with literal posts and `cmd.txt` lines, last of all, after the native sliders (the Bosses select, `boss_rarity` on `subtab:gameplay`, issue #44, is the first; `oracle.mjs`'s `locate` maps `subtab:<name>` to `#subtab-<name>`). `oracle-derive.test.js` fails when the committed file is not the derivation's output, and `npm run oracle:replay` fails its coverage check on an enumerated control that no oracle file lists.
   - A control that a pre-port legacy page did have, but that behaviour-oracle.json predates (the Gems of Incarnation switches and mod filter, which origin/main added to its legacy page after the port was recorded), is proven by recording that page instead: `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle-gems.json`, recorded with `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run oracle:record:gems -- --src <dir> --source-rev <sha>` from `git archive <sha> src` extracted outside the checkout, replayed by `npm run oracle:replay` through `--supplement`, and fed to the derivation with `--supplement` for its Turn off steps. Never edit it, and re-record it only from the same `sourceRev`. A key slider a later origin/main adds to `KEYS` (Prime Evil Parts, 1.4.7) is proven the same way, by `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle-primeevil.json` recorded from main's page (`oracle:record:primeevil`, replayed and derived through `--key-supplement`), and the reset line the backend then adds to every full key reset in the older recordings goes into `insertAddedKeys` in `panel/tests/lib/oracle-relocate.mjs`, never into the recordings.
   - After any edit under `panel/`, rebuild the panel from the hub root with `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run build` (`npm --prefix ForgePact/panel ci` first on a fresh checkout). `src/forgepact.py` serves, and `build_release.py` packages, whatever `panel/dist/` holds, so an edit that was not rebuilt is not what the browser tools, the oracle replay or a packaged `ForgePact.exe` see.
   - A new Mods-tab row goes in `itemsCard` only if it does something for a specific
     item the player forged in the Item Editor with that Mechanic - tell by whether
     its description begins "For an item (or amulet) forged with Mechanic: <name>".
     A row that changes how the game's own monsters are made, in every zone, goes in
     `gameplayCard` ("Gameplay", the third sub-tab, issue #44; today it holds only
     the Bosses select, `boss_rarity`, and `test_mods_categories.py` pins exactly
     that, so a second Gameplay row moves that pin too).
     Every other Mods-tab row goes in `qolCard` ("Quality of Life"). A row with a
     child (like Map Reveal's pack pass or Auto-prospect's material move) also needs
     its child row added to `preparePanelUI`'s parent/child grouping list for the
     card it lands in. Each top-level row (a parent together with its children)
     is drawn as its own card in the Mods columns, and none of the three Mods panels
     (Quality of Life, Items, Gameplay) carries a heading of its own: the sub-tab
     strip names them. `test_mods_categories.py`
     (issue #12) turns this rule into a check. A new Mods card also needs a sub-tab button in `#modsSubtabs` whose
     `aria-controls` names it - `ModsSubtabMarkupTests` fails if the two sets
     (sub-tab buttons and Mods cards) disagree.
4. **Execute Contract Tests:**
   - Run the full Python test suite to verify contract adherence. The parallel
     runner runs exactly the tests serial discovery runs, one worker per module,
     in about a third of the time (see the Command Reference):
     ```powershell
     py -3 tools/run_tests_parallel.py
     ```
     `py -m unittest discover -s tests -v` is the serial equivalent, and stays
     the reference: the two must print the same `Ran N tests` and status lines.
5. **Package Release Distribution (`build_release.py`):**
   - Run the packaging script:
     ```powershell
     py build_release.py
     ```
  - The packaging guard requires `plugin_build\BloodPactPlugin_ship.dll` to exist and confirms that `modfiles_shipped\BloodPactPlugin.dll` matches it. A missing or stale staged plugin stops packaging so the Install button cannot ship an older DLL.
6. **Write Release Notes (`release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md`, preferred but no longer a gate on tagging):**
   - Every version with player-visible changes should still get a `release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md` file at the ForgePact repo root, written in the PR that makes the change. This is the **preferred source**: it is player language, written by whoever made the change, while the change is fresh.
   - **Every Friday release's notes file names its release date**, on a line of its own under the heading: `Release date: YYYY-MM-DD`. ForgePact releases on Fridays. A version ending in `.0` is a **Friday release**: it moves exactly one minor or one major step from the previous `v*` tag (from 2.0.0 to 2.1.0 or 3.0.0), and its date must be a Friday. A version ending in anything else (2.0.1) is a **hotfix**: it keeps the previous tag's major and minor, and needs no date at all; one it does give may be any day, but must still be a single real date. `cut_release.py --check` fails a Friday release's notes file with no date, and any notes file with two dates, an impossible date, or a Friday release dated on another day. `forgepact_tag.py` refuses to tag a Friday release before its date, or on any day but a Friday when it has no notes file; any day from the date on is accepted, so a missed Friday can still ship late. Hotfixes are never held back. The day is read on Turkey's clock (UTC+03:00, the easternmost of the maintainers' timezones), so a release may go out once it is Friday there, even while it is still Thursday in Poland. Why: the owner, 2026-09-28: each release is on Friday and should not be released before it; releases by 0.0.1 are hotfixes and can go out any time; and, the same day, a 0.0.1 release's notes should not need a date.
   - **The files are temporary, and deleting them is automatic.** Publishing a (non-pre)release runs `forgepact-notes-cleanup.yml`, which asks `forgepact_tag.py --published-notes --version <v>` for every notes file at or below that version (the release's own and every skipped version it rolled up; anything older was carried by an earlier release), `git rm`s them and commits to `main` as the bot, rebasing and retrying up to three times if `main` moved. The published release page is then the record (git history keeps the file), and `--compose-notes` only reads versions newer than the previous tag, so nothing reads a published version's file again. It refuses a tag whose release is still a draft. Only unpublished versions' notes are ever at the repo root; v1.3.1–v1.3.16's were deleted by hand before the workflow existed (ForgePact#27). Its bot push does not fire `notify-hub.yml`, so the hub pointer picks the deletion up with the next ordinary merge. If a run fails, re-run "ForgePact notes cleanup" from Actions with the tag; don't delete the files by hand. A release event runs the workflows **in the tagged commit**, so a tag cut before a commit that carries this workflow does not start it on publish (v1.3.20 is the one such tag); run it by hand for that release. Verified live 2026-09-16: a manual run with the draft `v1.3.20` refused at "The release is published", and one with `v1.3.16` reported nothing to delete and committed nothing.
   - **Check the version is still unpublished before you leave notes sitting in a long-lived PR**, with `git tag --list vX.Y.Z` (and, if in doubt, `gh release list`). A branch that has been open across a release ends up carrying notes for a version that already shipped: the cleanup above then deletes them without them ever reaching a release page, and `--compose-notes` never selects them because it only reads the tagged version's own file plus versions newer than the previous tag. Re-file them under the next unpublished patch instead — and prefer the version another open PR is already using, so both features' notes ship with the release that carries the code; a textual conflict in one markdown file is cheaper than notes that go out silently missing. (2026-09-20: the toggle-skills PR's notes were on `v1.4.4`, published the day before, and moved to `v1.4.5`.)
   - It is no longer a prerequisite to tagging or releasing. `forgepact-tag.yml` composes the draft release body from whatever notes files exist at tag time — the tagged version's own file if it exists, otherwise GitHub's generated notes under a "rewrite for players before publishing" banner, plus every skipped version's own file concatenated in newest-first order. See "Tagging a release (forgepact-tag.yml)" below for the full composition rules. `cut_release.py --check` still fails on a missing notes file by default; only `--allow-missing-notes`, which only the tag workflow passes, relaxes that.
   - If the top file is missing at tag time, the draft's top section is generated notes under that banner, and it **must be rewritten into player language before publishing** — generated notes are pull-request titles, not something written for a player deciding whether to update.
   - Player-facing only, in plain language — what was broken and what changed *for the player*, not internal refactors, build-script fixes, or debugging history (that belongs in this instructions.md, e.g. Known Limitations, not in release notes). Match the tone of the existing files: name the symptom before the fix ("Tyrant's Crown and Monster Rarity did nothing in 1.3.14" before explaining why), and give a measured before/after number when one exists.
   - Standard sections, in order: `## New`, `## Fixed` (either may be omitted if empty, but at least one must be present), then `## How to update` with the standard boilerplate (see any existing file). A `## Changed` section is used for reorganizations (e.g. a control moving to a different panel tab) that are neither strictly new nor a bug fix.
   - Never claim something is "Fixed" that is not actually resolved. If an investigation concluded the *reported* symptom is not this project's bug (e.g. a freeze traced to a display driver / GPU stall with a control run proving the plugin was not involved), that finding belongs in this instructions.md's Known Limitations, not in release notes as a fix — release notes are read by players deciding whether to update, and an overclaimed fix erodes trust in every note that follows it.
7. **Write the panel's mod descriptions for the player, not as a coverage report:**
   - The small grey text under each mod in the panel (`src/forgepact.py`) says, in one or two plain sentences, what the mod does for the player, plus at most one caveat a player would act on (off by default, toggles excluded, and the like). Keep it to about 300 characters.
   - Measurement status, which skills were tested or covered by rule, measured values, edge cases and mid-cast quirks belong in the README row, the release notes and `docs/*-research.md`, which is where the honesty tests require them. Do not add tests that force that detail into the panel span; pin the span short, name-free and without overclaim instead.
   - Why: on 2026-09-22 the owner read the Timed skill countdown's panel text, which listed every coverage tier, the 0.2 s hit refresh and the mid-cast latch, and asked for it to "say what it should be not what it is exactly to the t with all the dev logs". The span became: "Shows how much time a timed skill has left, over that skill's slot on the skill bar, in the look you pick below. Works for most timed skills; toggles and companions (turrets, totems) don't get one. Off by default." (`SkillTimerRuleContractTests.test_player_text_states_behaviour_without_overclaim` scopes the detail words to README and release notes; `SkillTimerBuffContractTests.test_player_text_says_measured_buff_skills_are_covered_without_names` caps the panel span at 300 characters).

## Supported Platforms & Prerequisites

### Supported Platforms
- **Operating System:** Windows 10 / Windows 11 (64-bit x86_64).
- **Target Game:** Hero Siege Season 10 (offline, EAC disabled / single-player copy).

### Build & Development Prerequisites
- **Python:** Python 3.10+ (standard `py` launcher on Windows).
- **Node.js (panel build, since the UI port):** Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ (`panel/package.json`'s `engines`; release CI uses Node 22) with npm. Needed to build `panel/dist/`, which `build_release.py` refuses to package without and which `py src/forgepact.py` serves; running the Python contract tests alone does not need it. `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel ci` installs the pinned devDependencies from `panel/package-lock.json`.
- **Microsoft Edge (panel browser tests):** `panel/tests/*.mjs` drive the installed Edge through `playwright-core` (`channel: 'msedge'`, headless) and download no browser; the standard install path is enough. Without Edge, the browser-suite modules (`tests/test_panel_oracle_replay.py`, `tests/test_panel_e2e*.py` and `tests/test_panel_perf.py`) skip and say so, through `tests/panel_browser.py`'s `_missing()`.
- **C++ Compiler:** Microsoft Visual C++ (MSVC) supporting `/std:c++20`. `build.bat` finds it
  itself, in order: an already-initialised `vcvars` environment (`VSCMD_VER` defined and `cl`
  on `PATH`), then `vswhere -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64`
  (what finds VS 18.9 Enterprise on the `forgepact-release.yml` runner, `windows-2025-vs2026`,
  which none of the four legacy hardcoded paths below it match), then those four hardcoded
  paths (VS 18 BuildTools, VS 18 Community, VS 2022 Community, VS 2022 BuildTools) as a last
  resort. No manual setup needed if any of the three applies.
- **YYToolkit Headers and third-party binaries:** the `YYToolkit/`, `Aurie/`, `FunctionWrapper/`
  include trees, `YYTK_Shared_Types.cpp` (all under `plugin_build/include/`), and
  `modfiles_shipped/{AurieCore.dll,AuriePatcher.exe,YYToolkit.dll,HSOfflineTrackerProducer.dll}`.
  `py tools/fetch_toolchain.py` places all eleven pinned files, downloading each from a pinned
  commit or release and verifying its SHA-256 before writing anything (all-or-nothing: one bad
  hash writes nothing at all). `--verify-only` checks what's already there without downloading;
  `--force` replaces a hand-placed file that differs from the pin (the common case: a
  maintainer's own CRLF `Aurie/shared.hpp` copied in before this tool existed). See
  `tools/toolchain-pins.json` for exactly where each file comes from, and "The build half
  (forgepact-release.yml)" below for the full pin table. `origin`'s pin now names a `YYToolkit.dll`
  built from the hub's `third_party/yytoolkit/` series with `tools/build_yytoolkit.py`; the pull
  request that moved it from the previous `bb113eef…` file has merged (see the pin table's
  provenance note), but no ForgePact release has shipped a package built against the new pin yet,
  so a player's installed copy still runs `bb113eef…`.
- **hs-game-sdk:** required by **both** builds, not just the plugin. `build.bat` compiles against `hs-game-sdk/cpp/include` (`/I ..\..\hs-game-sdk\cpp\include`), and since 2026-09-14 `build_release.py` also puts `hs-game-sdk/python` on PyInstaller's analysis path — the panel imports `hs_game_sdk` for the Satanic Zone buff/debuff pool, and a package built without it ships that section empty. Building from inside a full toolkit checkout (ForgePact sits next to `hs-game-sdk/`) needs no extra setup; building ForgePact standalone means checking the hub out alongside it.
- **Python Packages (Optional / Packaging):**
  - `pyinstaller` (required for running `build_release.py`).
  - `pywebview` (optional; if installed, panel launches in a native desktop window, otherwise falls back to the default web browser).
  - `requirements-build.txt` pins the exact versions CI builds with (`pyinstaller==6.22.2`, `pywebview==6.2.1`); `py -3 -m pip install -r requirements-build.txt` reproduces them locally when matching a CI-built zip.

## Command Reference

| Command | Working Directory | Shell / Platform | Prerequisites | Expected Result | Side Effects | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `py src/forgepact.py` | `ForgePact/` | PowerShell / CMD | Python 3.10+ | Launches local control panel HTTP server (`http://127.0.0.1:8780`, or the next free of 8801, 8899, 9133, 9777). | Opens web browser / desktop window; watches for game process | Verified |
| `py -3 tools/run_tests_parallel.py` | `ForgePact/` | PowerShell / CMD | Python 3.10+ (stdlib only) | **The full-suite command.** Runs every Python contract test (including the native behavior harnesses, which skip without a C++ toolchain) with one worker process per test module, `-j` defaulting to `os.cpu_count()`, longest module first, except that a module declaring `PARALLEL_EXCLUSIVE = True` (`test_panel_perf.py`, the frame-budget suite, and `test_incident_monitor_behavior.py`, whose per-mod accounting times wall-clock spins) runs last with no other worker beside it, and the panel browser-suite modules (nine since 2026-09-28; `PARALLEL_GROUP = "panel-browser"`) run at most four at a time (`--group-limit panel-browser=<n>` overrides). `--exclude-module <name>` (repeatable, fnmatch patterns allowed) leaves modules out and says which: for a verify whose other criteria already run the panel's browser suites, `py -3 tools/run_tests_parallel.py --exclude-module "test_panel_e2e*" --exclude-module test_panel_oracle_replay --exclude-module test_panel_perf` checks everything else once. `--only-group <name>` runs just the modules declaring that `PARALLEL_GROUP` and `--skip-group <name>` everything else, so the two runs cover the suite exactly once between them; a group no module declares is not refused (`--skip-group` then runs everything, `--only-group` nothing), because release CI runs main's copy of this runner against older tagged trees. Release CI (`forgepact-release.yml`) runs `--skip-group panel-browser --exclude-module test_panel_perf` in its `build` job and `--only-group panel-browser` in its `panel-browser-tests` job, and leaves `test_panel_perf` to the local run (see "The build half (forgepact-release.yml)"). Prints unittest's own `Ran N tests in Xs` and `OK (skipped=K)` / `FAILED (...)` lines, with each failure's traceback; exits 1 on any failure, error, crashed worker or unexpected success, and **2 if the test ids the workers loaded are not exactly the ids serial discovery found** (less any modules `--exclude-module` or a group selection left out), or if an `--exclude-module` name matches no module. `-v` prints a line per module; `--list` prints the ids. | Writes `build/test-durations.json` (per-module wall time, used to order the next run) and, for a failing module only, its full worker output to `build/test-logs/<module>.log` | Verified 2026-09-27 on a 12-logical-core machine, with `panel/dist` built so every browser suite runs: 1650 tests, OK, skipped=8, **650 s** wall (`test_panel_perf` about 395 s of it, alone at the end; the six browser suites about 259 s, four at a time; everything else under a minute). With `--exclude-module "test_panel_e2e*" --exclude-module test_panel_oracle_replay --exclude-module test_panel_perf`: 1643 tests, OK, **55.5 s** over two runs. Before the browser suites were split into their own modules, the same machine took 1143 s (1642 tests; `test_panel_oracle` 735 s on one worker, then `test_panel_perf` 396 s). Serial `py -3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is unchanged by the split: 1292 s locally (1635 tests at `510f21e`), and 1449 s in `forgepact-release.yml`'s Contract tests step on the same commit (run 36307787871). Earlier, 2026-09-26, without the browser suites: 1559 tests, OK, skipped=8, 61-65 s wall over four runs (serial: 168-201 s). CPU averaged 88% during the run, so what remains is the harnesses' MSVC compiles (each `vcvars64.bat` alone is about 2 s); `-j 6`, `-j 8` and `-j 16` measured 70, 65 and 64 s on the same day's 1550-test tree. Without `-s` it runs ForgePact's `tests/` from `ForgePact/` wherever it is invoked, so `py -3 ForgePact/tools/run_tests_parallel.py` from the hub root is the same run |

## Data Formats, Persistence & IPC Contracts

### 1. Panel Configuration (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Hero_Siege\forgepact.json`)
Stores user UI settings in JSON format:
```json
{
  "exe": "C:\\Games\\HeroSiege\\Hero_Siege.exe",
  "auto_apply": true,
  "density": 1.5,
  "rift": 5,
  "battlefield": 1,
  "dungeon": 2,
  "relic": 1,
  "exp": 2.0,
  "magicfind": 1.5,
  "movespeed": 1.0,
  "damage": 25,
  "map_reveal": true,
  "map_reveal_packs": true,
  "headhunter": true,
  "tyrant": false,
  "beacon": false,
  "mod_filter_max_relics": false,
  "mod_orb_pickup_radius": false,
  "mod_pet_quest_pickup": false,
  "mod_toggle_indicator": false,
  "mod_toggle_guard": false,
  "switches": { "stats.exp": false, "rarity_rare": false },
  "theme": "default"
}
```

`switches` holds each slider's on/off switch (the enabled-mods workorder,
2026-09-25). A key is the slider's id: `"<section>.<key>"` for every row of
`STATS`, `PERCENT_STATS`, `SPAWNERS`, `DROPS` and `KEYS`, or the bare key for
the four top-level sliders `rarity_rare`, `rarity_ancient`, `angelic_items`
and `enemy_speed` - 40 ids, listed as `SLIDER_SWITCH_IDS` in
`src/forgepact.py`. Only **off** entries are stored (`false`); an absent id
means on, so a config written before switches existed (`DEFAULTS["switches"]`
is `{}`) reads as every switch on. Density has no entry: `density_on` has
always been its switch, and `enemy_speed_ct` is a scope, not a value. A
switch never changes the slider's saved value. `effective_cfg(cfg)` is a copy
in which every slider whose switch is off holds its `DEFAULTS` value, and
`build_cmds` (Apply and the launch watcher) runs over that copy, so off
behaves exactly like "slider at its default" and on restores the remembered
value. `/api/set` takes `{"section":"switches","key":<id>,"value":<bool>}`
(an id outside `SLIDER_SWITCH_IDS` answers 400 `{"err":"unknown switch"}`)
and, with the game running, sends exactly what that slider's own `/api/set`
branch sends for the effective value; no new command kind exists. A slider
moved while its switch is off saves the new value and sends the default's
command, as density does.

`rarity_rare` and `rarity_ancient` are the World › Monster Rarity shares, in
percent of the normal monsters: `rarity_rare` raises them to `enemyRarity` 3
and `rarity_ancient` to rank 4 (`rarity <rank3> <rank4>`). Since #159 the panel
labels those rows **Ancient** and **Legion**, the names the game shows for
ranks 3 and 4 (hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 13.7); before, they read
"Rare" and "Ancient", one tier too low. The keys, element ids, command and
plugin variables (`g_RarRarePct`, `g_RarAncientPct`) kept their old names so
saved settings carry over, and `tests/test_monster_rarity_labels.py` pins both
halves. The Bosses select (`boss_rarity` `rare`/`ancient`), Tyrant's Crown and
Beacon still say rare for rank 3 (#161).

`theme` is the panel's theme name (`DEFAULTS["theme"] = "default"`), painted
as `data-theme` on the page's root element. `/api/set`
`{"key":"theme","value":<name>}` accepts a name matching
`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}` (400 `{"err":"invalid theme"}` otherwise), stores it
and sends no command. `/api/state` keeps its shape; `cfg` carries both keys.

Note `map_reveal_packs`: it is the only key that defaults to **true** while its
parent (`map_reveal`) defaults to false, because the plugin also defaults its
pack flag on. `build_cmds` therefore emits `reveal packs 0` only to turn it
*off*, and the panel restates the child whenever the parent is switched back on
(otherwise a player who turned packs off would silently get them back).

### 2. IPC Command File (`<game>\bin\bp_ipc\cmd.txt`)
UTF-8 / ASCII plain-text command queue. The panel appends lines to `cmd.txt`; the plugin reads, executes, and clears the file every few frames.
- Example commands:
  - `ping`: Keepalive and synchronization probe.
  - `density 2.0`: Sets enemy density multiplier to 2.0x.
  - `specialrate rift 5`: Sets Rift Portal spawner multiplier to 5x.
  - `droprate group dungeon 2`: Sets Dungeon Key drop multiplier.
  - `dropmult gold <n>`: the Loot tab's **Gold** slider. **Since 2.0.1 (issue #77) it multiplies the amount of the one coin, not the number of coins**; every other `dropmult` target still runs the game's own drop script `<n>` times (`DropManager.hpp`). `DropGold` and `DropMonsterGold` have their own hook bodies instead of `FP_DROP_HOOK`: `DropMonsterGold`'s original runs exactly once whatever the multiplier, and `DropGold`'s original runs once with argument 4 (`kDropGoldAmountArg`, the coin's amount: the one argument that varied per coin in Live 1's `goldtrace`) replaced by a scaled copy - the caller's own `RValue` is never written. At x1, and inside AFK FARM's `RewardScope`, the arguments pass through untouched. Log lines, once a session each: `dropmult gold: x<n> applied to the coin's amount (one coin per drop): first coin <a> -> <a*n>` the first time it scales, and `dropmult gold: x<n> not applied - DropGold's amount (argument 4) was missing|not a finite number (kind <k>); the coin keeps the game's amount` when it cannot (counted every time, `GoldUnscaledCount()`). And one line per coin for the first 8 coins after each change of the configured multiplier (the first ones of a session too, at x1, once the hook is in): `dropmult gold coin <i>/8 at x<n>: argument 4 <handed> -> <passed on> (arguments 1,2: <x>, <y>)`, with ` (reward scope; set x<m>)` after the multiplier when AFK FARM's scope held it at x1. These are the positive control on argument 4 being the amount the game credits: the hook only proves what `DropGold` was handed, so a gold reading taken before and after picking up one coin is held against that coin's line (at x1 the delta should equal it; at x100, about 100 times). Live 2 (2026-09-27, player DLL `c36004c6...8e6b`) read `first coin 44 -> 4400` at x100 beside a HUD gold rise of 12870 over two stacks, with no freeze (Known Limitations item 32). Before the fix the two count hooks nested: x100 ran the monster-gold original 100 times, each reaching a `DropGold` hook that ran its own 100 times, so 10,000 coins per monster gold drop (Known Limitations item 32).
  - `dungeonkey add 12 1` / `dungeonkey on`: Opens outer LoadDrops gate for Dungeon Keys (type 12).
  - `stat damage 1.25`: Sets damage multiplier to 1.25 (+25%).

Safe to send at launch: it arms the mod and the `GetRelicQuest` hook is installed later, once a player instance exists, as a native detour or not at all (`relicfilter: hook installed -> ON (GetRelicQuest, native detour)`, else `FAILED (...)`).

Each skip logs `relicfilter: skipped maxed relic <id>, the game picks again (<n> since armed)`, the first 20 one by one and then every 100th; with every droppable relic maxed it logs `relicfilter: every droppable relic is maxed, filter stands down (nothing left to drop instead)` once per change.

To see which relic a drop built, place relics with `callnum DropRelic <x> <y> 0 0 1 0` (a true fifth argument skips the chance roll) and count `CreateItemNew`'s research-log lines in `bp_ipc\itemdrops.jsonl` (class 16, by `b`). The equipped-slot report is the SDK's `FormatEquippedSlotScanReport` of the equipped-slot read (`mplr=`, `slots=`, `inrange=`, `strings=`, `owner=`, `resolved=`, `refused=`, `nonstruct=`, `noclass=`, `relic=`, `otherclass=`, `relics=<slot>:<id>@<level>,...`, the helmet-slot positive control `control=` and `itemType=`, and `stopped=<stage|none>`), so a zero says whether the relic slots 10-14 were read at all. Measured in Live 1 (2026-09-27): `scan found 3 maxed relics (ids 109,124,135)` with `mplr=1 slots=18 inrange=5 strings=5 owner=ok resolved=5 refused=0 ... relic=5 ... control=resolved itemType=0 stopped=none`, the five `slot:id@level` pairs equal to the save's. The `LootGroundCreateFromItem` route is `sigdrop`'s and `angelicdrop`'s, measured on the ground 30/30 and 17/17 (2026-09-18), but always with the dying enemy as `self` and never for a relic, which is why each placement is read back. Since 1.3.20 `FrameCallback` *scans* for globe instances every `kOrbScanFrames` (15) frames — or sooner once the player has travelled the whole approach budget, which is what keeps the scan correct at 10x Movement Speed — and *pulls* the cached ones every frame toward the player at a constant `kGlobePullSpeed` (6 px/frame — tuned down from an accelerating ramp per user feedback 2026-09-10, which snapped the last stretch in a single frame and read as an unnatural teleport); the game's own pickup logic then fires normally once close enough. `orbpickup stat` (also printed when the mod is switched off) reads as a decision tree: `seen=0` while standing next to globes means the object indices are wrong, `noplayer>0` means the player never resolved, and only `outofreach` means the radius is too small — `nearest=` says by how much. `seen`, `noplayer` and `outofreach` are each counted once per globe per **scan** so they stay comparable with one another; `pulled` is per frame.     - `reveal` clears the zone's minimap fog grid once per zone identity - measured 2026-09-11 to be all that static icons need (waypoints, dungeon entrances, chests, shrines and mining nodes are fog-gated, **not** gated by `isDiscovered`, so no per-object sweep exists or is needed).
    - `reveal packs` is the monster half and the only part that adds work: most packs do not exist until the player walks within ~1050 px of their `Enemy_Creator_*`, so it opens a bounded 900-frame window per zone during which `distance_to_object` answers 0 for creators, letting the game's own creator logic populate the map (measured 148 → 866 and 208 → 1273 enemies; ~7.8 ms frame average, plugin 2.3%).
    - The window only opens once a live creator reports a real `enemyCreatorTimer` - firing during zone load leaves spawners permanently inert.
    - **The authorization is then re-checked per creator, inside `Hook_distance_to_object`, at the moment the distance would be changed** - not at a frame boundary: `EVENT_FRAME` is dispatched from `HkPresent` at the end of the frame, while creators consume the permission in their step events earlier in the same frame, so a window invalidated at Present is too late for the first call in a new zone.
    - A creator that has not initialised keeps its real distance however stale the window is; a ready one is still served, so the pass keeps working across a transition instead of failing closed.
    - The same guard covers the Beacon's lie.
    - The window is additionally bound to the full zone identity (room + minimap instance + grid), re-checked every frame as defence in depth, and is never opened against an identity that could not be read.
    - Turning `reveal packs` on arms the **current** zone's readiness-gated pass rather than waiting for the next zone change.

  - `petquest 1` / `petquest 0` (+ `petquest stat` in the research build only): Pet Quest Collector. Working and live-measured 2026-09-11. While enabled and a `Companion_obj` exists, `FrameCallback` runs a two-phase tick: `Idle` enumerates `Quest_Object_Parent_obj` descendants inside the camera view (minus a static exclusion list, 64-instance budget per tick, starting where the last tick's walk stopped and wrapping, so every instance is read within a few ticks), picks the nearest collectable one that is not held back (`PetQuestSelector` in `PetQuestCollectorMod.hpp`, the 2.0.1 target-selection change), and `Travel` writes the pet's `x`/`y` toward it at 11 px/frame until it arrives (or 240 frames elapse, which collects anyway - the walk is cosmetic, the credit is the point), then invokes the collect and waits 24 frames. A travel that ends with the item still in place - the collect dispatched and the item remained, a gate refused it at arrival, the call was refused, or the travel timed out and the collect-anyway did not remove it - holds that item back for `kPetQuestHoldFrames` (600) ticks, so the next pick is another item; with every item on screen held back the pet waits. `petquest 0` (both builds) prints the counter lines: `petquest stat: family objs seen=… excluded=… on-screen=…`, `  collected=… | skipped(gate)=… skipped(no Loot_Manager)=… | target lost=… travel timeouts=… | held back=… | phase=… arg=…` (`held back=` counts every hold since load) and `  call route=… | dispatched-but-item-remained=…`. The collect: with the item as `self` and `Loot_Manager_obj` as `other`, invoke the item's own `m_Questpickup` method value with one real argument, reached via `InvokeMethodValue` (the callable read off the method value's own `CScriptRef`, validated before the call — no game addresses; see Known Limitations item 11); it calls `update_quest` -> `QuestSaveUpdate` internally, so the objective credit is inside the call and nothing is faked. The game's own gates (`canPickup`, `lootType == 0`) are re-read from the live instance at collect time. `petquest arg <n>` (both builds) changes the one argument that was reproduced rather than understood. **Not implemented:** an accepted-quest gate, and the loot-system side effects a real collect performs (sound, pickup effect, inventory log) - so a pet collect is silent. See `ForgePact/docs/pet-quest-collector-c-research.md` and Known Limitations item 11.

The game's own companion loot pickup, not the Pet Quest Collector. While enabled, `FrameCallback` runs `PetLootUnstickTick()`: it finds the first `Companion_obj` (resolved by name, SDK constant as fallback), reads its `lootTarget` as a number, and feeds `PetLootStuckWatch` the target id and the pet-to-target distance. It also reads the target's `object_index` first and answers the header's `PetLootRoute`: a live target from neither `Loot_Ground_obj` nor `Coin_obj` is dropped on the tick that sees it (a stale id the game reused - Live 2 - counted `other kind=` with the index), because it can never be picked up and waiting out the watch would leave the pet grinding at it. When the same live target has stayed within 160 px for 90 consecutive frames (and again every 90 frames while a target taken straight back stays in reach: the watch re-arms at each give-up), the tick writes `itemCompanionTimer` = 600 on the target if it is a `Loot_Ground_obj` and `variable_instance_exists` says it carries that name (the game's own "not for the pet yet" timer; a ground item without it gets nothing written and is counted `timer absent=`; a `Coin_obj` has none and is only released), sets the pet's `lootTarget` to -4, and empties the pet's `lootList` with `ds_list_clear` when `ds_exists(lootList, ds_type_list)` confirms it is a live list, so the game's next half-second scan picks something else. No hook, no game script called, nothing collected or destroyed. `petunstick 0` prints one line: `petunstick stat: held back=<n> coins released=<n> longest same-target=<n> frames`, then `ticks=`, `no pet=`, `no target=`, `target gone=`, `unreadable=` and `list not cleared=` (each refusal with the read it failed on), then `give-up failed=`, `other kind=`, `timer absent=` and `re-picked while held=` (a given-up target taken back within the hold, after leaving it or straight back on the next tick, counted once per give-up by the header's `PetLootRepickRing`) with its `(ground <n> coin <n>)` split and the last ground timer read back (`FullStatLine()` followed by `PetLootLocalStatSuffix()`). See Known Limitations item 37.

A player command with one branch in the dispatcher, separate from `petquest`. While enabled, `FrameCallback` runs `PetRelicCollectorTick()` right after the quest collector's tick: with a `Companion_obj` out, `Idle` lists the `Loot_Ground_obj` instances on screen, keeps those `HeroSiege::Player::ReadGroundRelic` identifies as relics, drops every one whose relic id is in the maxed set (the local player's owned relic levels through `HeroSiege::Player::GetOwnedRelicLevels`, stored only when both the equipped-slot and the relic-tab scan report `stopped == nullptr`, re-read at most once per 60 ticks and straight after a collect that returned true, plus `relicfilter testmaxed`'s ids; with no complete read yet the tick picks nothing and counts `refused=` `maxed-scan-incomplete(<scan>:<stage>)`), and picks through its own `PetQuestSelector` when `PetFetchArbiter` lets it; `Travel` is `PetTravelStep`, the walk the quest tick also uses. On arrival `PetRelicCollectOne` re-reads eligibility (relic, not maxed, `itemActive` not false - a missing name is counted, not refused), reads the owned level of that relic id again, whole (an incomplete read refuses the collect), and calls `gml_Script_PickupLoot` by name with `self` = the ground relic, `other` = the pet, and `global.mplr`, the relic's `itemInstance`, `true`, `true` and its `isPlayerDrop` through `GetVariable` (the companion's own call, research doc § "The companion's call"); route B (research only) calls `gml_Script_PickupRelic(mplr, itemInstance)` with the same `self`/`other`. A false return or a throw destroys nothing and holds the relic back; the first eight refusals each log `petrelic: collect refused (<why>) supplied: ... Nothing was destroyed.`. A true return is not taken as a pickup by itself (a relic-tab copy at 10/10 also answers true and raises nothing): the plugin reads the owned levels again, whole, and only when that relic's level is exactly one higher, or the id is newly owned, does it destroy the ground relic itself (`instance_destroy`, since neither pickup script does) and count `collected=`; otherwise it destroys nothing, holds the relic back and logs `petrelic: pickup returned true, relic left on the ground (<why>); held back.` for the first eight. `petrelic 0` prints the `petrelic stat:` line (`StatLine()`). See Known Limitations item 46.

The first `jumpscenery 1` installs the six hooks by name (`skillsLeap` through `HookOneScript`, refused unless its inline detour went in; the five collision builtins through `HookBuiltin`); if any fails it prints `jumpscenery: refused - <why>` and the mod stays off. `jumpscenery 1` / `0` print `jumpscenery: on` / `jumpscenery: off`; bare `jumpscenery` or `stat` prints the one stat line (Command Reference). The modstate JSON carries `"jumpScenery":{"enabled":...}`.
  - `hiddenloot 1` / `hiddenloot 0` / `hiddenloot stat` / `hiddenloot key <vk>` (both builds; a player command in `kPlayerCommands` with its own early return in `RunCommand`; panel keys `mod_hidden_loot`, off by default, and `mod_hidden_loot_key`, 164 by default; `build_cmds` sends `hiddenloot key <vk>` and then `hiddenloot 1` only when the switch is on): Sleep loot your filter hides (#95 part 2b, `HiddenLootMod.hpp`, `docs/hidden-loot-research.md` § "The mod", "Hidden loot sleep (`hiddenloot`)" below). The first `hiddenloot 1` after setup (or the first tick after setup, if it came earlier) installs the `LootGroundInit` hook once; `FrameCallback` runs `HiddenLootTick()` after `FarSleepTick()`, which returns at once while off. The key is stored whether or not the mod is on, and read only while it is. The four line formats, which the live procedure reads byte for byte:
    - `hiddenloot 1` prints `hiddenloot -> ON route=<both|table-only|none> key=<vk|none> walk-slept=<n> walk-visible=<n> walk-no-filter-var=<n>` (the switch-on walk over the ground items already there). A table-only or failed install also logs `hiddenloot: LootGroundInit hook TABLE-ONLY` (or `not installed`) `- the game's own drop calls may pass it by, so a pass every 18 frames over the awake ground items puts hidden loot to sleep instead`.
    - `hiddenloot 0` prints `hiddenloot -> OFF woken=<n> exist-after=<n>` followed, on the same line, by the stat fields below.
    - `hiddenloot stat` prints `hiddenloot stat: on=<0|1> route=<..> key=<vk|none> held=<0|1> inits=<n> slept=<n> asleep-now=<n> shown-now=<n> visible=<n> no-filter-var=<n> unidentified=<n> gone=<n> passes=<n> skipped-persistent=<n> errors=<n> by-arg0=<n> by-arg1=<n> by-self=<n> reduced=<n> dropped=<n> kinds=<a0>/<a1>/<self> obj-a0=<n> obj-a1=<n> obj-self=<n> reduced-a0=<n> reduced-a1=<n> reduced-self=<n> not-instance-a0=<n> not-instance-a1=<n> not-instance-self=<n> no-id-a0=<n> no-id-a1=<n> no-id-self=<n> threw-a0=<n> threw-a1=<n> threw-self=<n>`. `inits` counts `LootGroundInit` calls seen while on; `slept` counts an item's first sleep from any path; `asleep-now` and `shown-now` are current; `visible`, `no-filter-var`, `unidentified` and `skipped-persistent` count items or calls left alone and why; `gone` counts shown or woken items no longer there (picked up); `passes` counts the fallback's walks. The six fields after `errors` (added with the in-call reduction, 2026-10-02) count the hook's handles: `by-arg0`, `by-arg1` and `by-self` count which of the call's values (argument 0, argument 1, `self`) identified the item at the frame's end; `reduced` counts instance pointers made into their own `id` inside the call, and `dropped` those that were not (`instance_exists` false, an `id` that is not a number, or a read that threw, which also counts in `errors`); `kinds` names the last call's three values as passed, before the reduction (`num`, `ref`, `obj`, `undef` or `other`; `-` before the first call). The fifteen fields after `kinds` split `reduced` and `dropped` per value (`a0` argument 0, `a1` argument 1, `self`) and per outcome, rows in the order `obj`, `reduced`, `not-instance`, `no-id`, `threw`: `obj-` counts the values that arrived as an object and so reached `instance_exists` at all, and the other four, which add up to it per value, count `instance_exists` true with a numeric `id` (`reduced-`), false (`not-instance-`; by the reading an item struct on argument 1, which Live 3 never saw arrive as an object, `obj-a1=0`; `lootspawn`'s `self`, the global instance, lands here), true with no numeric `id` (`no-id-`), and a read that threw (`threw-`, also in `errors`). They exist because `self`, a live instance on every monster drop, fills the `reduced` and `dropped` sums on its own: Live procedure 3's `struct-safe` reads `obj-a1` and `not-instance-a1`, with `reduced-self` as the positive control. `errors` also counts a call turned away at the pending cap.
    - `hiddenloot key <n>` prints `hiddenloot: key=<vk|none>`. It accepts 0 (none) or 3-254; 1, 2 and anything else print `hiddenloot: key refused - <why>; key stays <vk|none>`. Anything else prints `hiddenloot: usage hiddenloot 1 | 0 | stat | key <vk>`.
    - Once a session, if the game refused a write of the built-in `visible`: `hiddenloot: note - the game did not take a write of the built-in visible; shown items appear at the game's own filter refresh, within 0.3 s`. `modstate.json` carries `hiddenLoot`: `enabled`, `route`, `key`, `asleep`, `shown`, `held`, `errors`.

    - The box is **derived** from that slot's own live `navBboxX`/`navBboxY`/`navBboxWidth`/`navBboxHeight` (`x + 2.3`, `y` unchanged, `w - 4.7`, `h - 13.2`) and rounded to whole pixels per Known Limitations item 18 - the accepted `120 x 126 @388,1711` is evidence for one slot at one HUD scale, not a constant.
    - `toggleborder 0` prints `drawn=`/`on=`/`off=`/`unreadable=`/`noHud=`/`noRow0=`/`noTalent=`/`foreign=`/`drawExc=`/`unresolved=` - `noHud`/`noRow0`/`noTalent` are the three meaningfully different reasons `ToggleIndicatorFindSlot` can fail to find the slot (follow-up from the indicator's reviews; replaces a single `noSlot=`), `drawExc` counts a swallowed exception from the marker draw itself, and `unresolved` counts a row skipped because its `abilityId` has not been matched yet.
    - **Every counter on that line is a sum over every shipped row** - the draw visits each row once, so a player with nothing toggled reads `off=` at the row count times the number of draws - and both outputs say so, the line ending `(summed over 8 rows)`.
    - `toggleborder stat` (read-only, stores nothing) prints the same counters plus `enabled=on|off`, a second line with `<abilityId>:talentId=<n|unresolved>` per row, `resolveWalks=` and `unresolvedRows=`, and then **one line per row** naming it by its `abilityId` with that row's own `drawn=`/`on=`/`off=`/`unreadable=`/`unresolved=`/`noSlot=`/`subOff=`/`subUnreadable=` (the last two count draws where a sub-talent-gated row - today only Counter - read its sub-talent as not allocated or unreadable; they appear on the per-row lines only, not in the summed line) - which is what answers "which row was ON" and "which row lost its slot" (`noSlot` is the row-level view of the three HUD-side failures the summed line splits into `noHud`/`noRow0`/`noTalent`).

  - `toggleguard 1` / `toggleguard 0` / `toggleguard stat`: shipped toggle-skill re-cast guard (issue #11, Track A, T1, generalised in phase S).
    - `1` only arms it; `FrameCallback` installs `HookOneScript("TalentUseClass", …)` (`HookTalentUseClass`, both routes) once the setup gate has passed and `HhResolveLocalPlayer` succeeds, checked once a second - the `relicfilter` shape (Known Limitations item 8), so it is safe to send at launch.
    - While on, a `TalentUseClass` call whose caller's own `object_index` (read with `variable_instance_get` and `N1ObjectIndex`, which accepts the `VALUE_REF` this runner returns) equals `asset_get_index("Universal_Double_Cast_obj")` **and** whose first argument is the runtime-resolved talent id of one of the same seven rows the indicator covers (Soul Spurn, Lunar Orbit, Crematus, Submerged Knives, Maelstrom of Frost, Meteor Storm, Bushido) reaches the guard.
    - Six of the seven rows have a toggle sub-talent; **the refusal is gated on that sub-talent being allocated, read at the call** with the talent the call itself named: `global.subTalentMap[<index>]` → `t<talentId>` → `s<NN>` (the slot per row: `s12` Soul Spurn, `s11` Lunar Orbit, `s13` Crematus, `s13` Submerged Knives, `s11` Maelstrom of Frost, `s11` Meteor Storm).
    - **The array index is selected, not assumed**: session 6's measured index 1 is tried first and, if its entry carries no `t<talentId>` struct, the other indices (cap 16) are tried in turn and the first that does carry one answers - the struct's own presence is the positive signal, so an index that turns out to be a character or player slot on another save cannot leave the guard silently inert.
    - Each index is judged on its own (its entry's kind checked before it is read, its own `try`), so one junk entry in front of the real one costs that index and not the walk.
    - A numeric > 0 refuses - the hook returns without calling the original, the co-op puppet's early-return shape.
    - The measured unallocated form (`0.000000`, key present) passes and counts `subOff=`; the global missing, not an array, no index carrying `t<id>`, `s<NN>` absent or non-numeric, or a throw anywhere passes and counts `subUnreadable=`.
    - Everything else passes, and the toggle's own state is still never read (`docs/toggle-skills-research.md`, "Track A design (D-N1)" and "S design").
    - **Bushido (session 9, D-B1) is the seventh row and has no sub-talent at all - a toggle on its own** - so it is refused unconditionally, every time it is the caller and the double-cast proc names it, without ever reading `global.subTalentMap`: feeding a real slot's key space the row's `kToggleNoSubTalent` constant (0) would find no `t<id>` struct there and answer Unreadable, which would pass the proc through - the exact "reports armed and does nothing" shape.
    - Its refusals count in both `refused=` and a separate `baseForm=`.
    - A caller or object that cannot be read passes (fails open) and is counted; an unresolved row is not guarded at all.
    - `toggleguard 0` clears the flag only; the hook stays and passes every call through.
    - `toggleguard 0` and `toggleguard stat` (read-only) print `refused=`/`passed=`/`procSeen=`/`selfUnreadable=`/`objUnresolved=`/`subOff=`/`subUnreadable=`/`baseForm=`/`subIndex=<n|none>` (which `global.subTalentMap` index actually answered, so a moved map and an unallocated sub-talent are never the same silent counter)/`hook=not installed|installed|TABLE-ONLY`, `stat` also `enabled=` and the same per-row `talentId=` line `toggleborder stat` prints; the research build adds `lastProcRet=` (what the last passed proc call returned).

On that button only, `manualDisable` is read and, if it is closed (`true`), written `false` in the kind it was read in (the game's bool stays a bool), before the game's own body runs; `enabled` is never touched. Nothing is restored after the call: the game recomputes the member every frame. The first write logs `restartanytime: first write - …` once per session.

Research and rows: `ForgePact/docs/toggle-skills-research.md` (`### Buff-carried countdown (session 12)`).
  - `autoprospect 1` / `autoprospect 0` (+ `autoprospect stat` in the research build only; `autoprospect` is in `kPlayerCommands`, dispatched from `HandleProspectCommand`): Auto-prospect on insert (issue #9, Stage B; panel key `mod_auto_prospect`, off by default, `build_cmds` emits `autoprospect 1` only when it is on).
    - While on, every item moved into the Prospect Cube's grid - drag or click - is prospected at once by the game's own Prospect handler.
    - The decision is `ForgePact::AutoProspectMod` (`plugin/include/ForgePact/AutoProspectMod.hpp`, game-independent); the adapter in `ModuleMain.cpp` is a hook on `m_MoveItemToGrid` (`UI_Inventory_Grid_obj anon@15345`, through the SDK constant and `HookOneScript`'s two routes, installed once from `FrameCallback` after setup; it only tells the core an insert into the node whose `uiNodeCallstack` names `"ProspectGrid"` happened, and never invokes) plus `AutoProspectTick` in `FrameCallback`, entered only while the mod is on, which re-finds the window, the grid and - only while an insert is pending - the Prospect button (the `UI_Button_Small_obj` linked to the window whose `activationFunc` is a method of `UiAProspectButton`), and invokes the one shape Phase 1 recorded: `script_execute` through `CallBuiltinEx`, the handler's `asset_get_index` value and the button's own `activationArgs` array, `self` = the button, `other` = the window.
    - An insert invokes when the grid's filled count is above the count the core last *settled* (first sight, re-read straight after an invoke, a refused insert, an expired one - lowered by removals, never raised by an unreported fill), because a click-in's cell is filled before the insert closure runs (`contents=6->6`).
    - Replies: `autoprospect: armed - ...` then `autoprospect: hook installed -> ON`; a `TABLE-ONLY` or failed install turns it off (`autoprospect: hook TABLE-ONLY -> OFF: ...`), and `autoprospect 1` then answers `unavailable this session`.
    - Both builds log each refusal once per session (`no-window`, `no-grid`, `unreadable`, `node-changed`, `no-button`, `no-args`, `grid-full` - `holding back - N free cells, needs 6; empty some of the grid`), a failed dispatch once, `autoprospect: first prospect - invoked=… prospected=…` once, and once each the first invoke that dispatched but left the grid unchanged (`autoprospect: the Prospect ran but the grid did not change - invoked=… ran-no-effect=…`) and the first whose effect could not be read (`autoprospect: the Prospect ran but the grid could not be read afterwards - …`).
    - The drag-in fills its cells after the insert closure returns (`contents=0->0`, Phase 3 S1) and the click-in before it; the settled count covers both.
    - `autoprospect stat` prints `StatLine()` (`invoked`, `prospected`, `ran-no-effect`, `unverified`, `failed`, inserts with `coalesced`/`while-invoking`/`elsewhere`/`while-off`, `not-landed`, the refusal counts) and the hook state.
    - The research build also logs, unasked, five **`autoprospect research:`** lines (Stage D, for the ore that came back - `prospected` cannot tell an ore that went back to the bag from one that was prospected): `insert` (from the hook: `frame=`, whether it went into the ProspectGrid, `invoking=`, `self`/`other`, the argument kinds, the grid's filled count and fingerprints at hook time), `decide` (a move-pass decision: the view, the recorded batch before the decision consumed it - `AutoProspectMod::BatchList()`, a copy - and the named cells), `move` (per cell: fingerprint, `itemType`, `itemDefinitionStruct`, CanAdd's return, `route=stack|place|none`, `preferred=` - the new-type route's `GetItemPreferredGrid` return - the Add's or the place's return, clear, final read, outcome), `invoke` (dispatched, the view, the after-read, the new batch, the `inserted` fingerprints, the bag grid's count) and `fate` (the next tick: each inserted fingerprint `gone`/`still`, what `GetItemFromFingerprint(fp, 0)` returns for it now, whether the bag grid `InventoryGrid` holds it, and the bag's gained/lost fingerprints).
    - They are `ApResearch*` functions inside `#ifndef FORGEPACT_RELEASE`, each called from one research-only line of the adapter; the player build has none of them (`test_autoprospect_research_log_is_research_only`).
    - See Known Limitations item 19 and `ForgePact/docs/prospect-window-research.md` § Stage B ship design / § Stage B Phase 3 live procedure.
    - **`bp_ipc\modstate.json`** (both builds, written from the frame callback only when its text changes): `{"schemaVersion":1,"autoprospect":{"enabled","hookBlind","bagPreference","movePass","reason"}}`. The panel reads it (`plugin_mod_state`, `/api/state.pluginMods`) and paints `off (plugin)` with the reason beside a switch the plugin is refusing, and both auto-prospect change handlers re-read it before they toast - so a move pass that shut itself down for the session, or an insert hook that went in table-only, is visible in the panel instead of only in `out.txt` (review of ForgePact #54). The renderer's healthy branches repaint too - the parent label from its own switch, the child through `syncProspectBag` - so the poll clears `off (plugin)` by itself once a new session reports healthy, which is what the refusal's own message promises (follow-up review, ForgePact a604aa7).
- `autoprospect bag 1` / `autoprospect bag 0`: Auto-prospect's sub-option (issue #9, Stage C; panel key `mod_auto_prospect_bag`, nested under `mod_auto_prospect` the way `map_reveal_packs` sits under `map_reveal`; **on by default** in the core and the panel, so `build_cmds` emits `autoprospect bag 0` after `autoprospect 1` only when it is off, and turning the parent on live restates it; `autoprospect 1|0` leaves it alone).
  - With it on, the frame a landed insert is about to be prospected - only the free-cell check left - first moves the previous prospect's batch to the player's materials tab, then prospects in the same frame, so the newest batch stays visible.
  - The batch is what the core's own last invoke produced (round 1): `OnInvoked` records the fingerprints in the grid read straight after the call that were not in the invoking view (both reads share the frame, and `ApReadCells` fills the view's `printList` for each), so nothing the player inserts - an ore included, though it is a material - is in it, with one accepted corner (not observed): a batch stack the player swaps out and drops back in within `kAutoProspectLandFrames` keeps its batch fingerprint, so it goes to the tab rather than being prospected.
  - It is forgotten on first sight of a node (new node, window or grid gone, parent toggled), a removal, or a `not-landed` expiry, and consumed by the pass; a forgotten batch moves nothing.
  - The core returns `MoveMaterials` naming only the batch's cells that the adapter also flagged as materials, one per fingerprint (the item behind each filled cell's `nodeFingerprint`, looked up by the game's own `GetItemFromFingerprint`, with `itemType` equal to the SDK's `HeroSiege::Items::ItemType::Material`; read only on frames with a pending insert, the pass on and a recorded batch); `ApMovePass` then runs the route M7 recorded, per cell, by name through `script_execute` with self = other = the ProspectGrid node: the cell re-read and still holding the viewed fingerprint, `InventoryGridCanAddToStack(1, undefined, item)`, then - when it is truthy (an existing stack) - `InventoryGridAddToStack(1, item)` returning `success == true`, or - when it is falsy, which it is for every material whose type the tab holds no stack of (Stage D, the new-type route the game's own click-move takes, `prospect-window-research.md` § Stage D results) - `GetItemPreferredGrid(1, item)`, whose result must be a plain struct with an array `grid` member (`ApPreferredGrid`), then `GridAddItem(that grid, item, 0, undefined)` returning `success == true` (the same `ApAddSucceeded`), and only then, on the cell still holding the same fingerprint, `InvGridClearItemNode(cell, undefined)` - one clear site for both routes.
  - A new-type material lands in the **main bag grid** (`tabType` 0), where a click puts it, not the materials tab.
  - `g_AutoProspectInvoking` is held across the pass.
  - After it the tick re-reads everything and asks the core again; the landed insert stays landed even when the read is now at or below the settled count.
  - Outcomes, each counted and each non-moved reason logged once per session in both builds (the prospect still runs in every case): `moved` (and `moved-new` when the new-type route placed it), `no-preferred-grid` (a new type whose preferred-grid lookup ran and named no grid of the recorded shape; a lookup that never ran is `move-failed`), `not-placed` (the place ran without `success` and the cell is unchanged), `not-added`, `move-failed`, and `vanished` (the cell lost the material without `success`) or `cell-kept` (success, but the final read still holds it or could not be made) - either of the last two turns the pass off for the session with a line saying so, after which `autoprospect bag 1` answers `bag unavailable this session`.

    - Output, exact bytes (the hub's parse contract, pinned by `tests/test_menu_layout_contract.py`): a header `menulayout: room=<Room> gui=<W>x<H> window=<W>x<H> fullscreen=<0|1> view=<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>`; one row per instance, two-space indent, `obj=<Obj> id=<id> gui=<x>,<y> win=<cx>,<cy> bbox=<l>,<t>,<r>,<b> visible=<0|1> sprite=<Sprite|none>`, then whichever of `label`, `name`, `slot`, `index`, `page`, `selected`, `uiNodeCallstack`, `activationArgs`, `enabled`, `tabNumber`, `tabType`, `stashTabSelected`, `tabSelected`, `nodeGridWidth`, `nodeGridHeight`, `gridScale`, `gridName` the instance carries (an array value as `[a,b,...]`, each element through the same formatter, the first 32 then `,...+N`, a nested array as `<array>`; a reference, struct or pointer by kind only, `<ref>`, `<object>` or `<ptr>`, any other non-scalar kind as `<kind N>`; `activationFunc` is never printed), then always last `text=<to end of line>` (empty when it has none); and a footer `menulayout: listed=<n> absent=<names|none> capped=<0|1>` (200 rows at most; a name that does not resolve is listed in `absent=`). After the stash and bag fields a row prints `talentId` when the instance carries it (a list of its own, so the stash list keeps its pinned order; live 2 of the skill research printed it on the talent buttons, the sub-skill buttons and the sub-panel and none of the six other candidates - `subTalentId`, `talentLevel`, `treeIndex`, `slotIndex`, `allocated`, `pointsAvailable` - on any row, so those were pruned). A `UI_Hud_Talent_obj` row is followed by one `  slot=<row>,<i> talent=<talentId|none> gui=<navBboxX>,<navBboxY> win=<cx>,<cy>` row per element of its `row0` and `row1` arrays (32 per array at most; `none` for a field the element does not carry, `<read-failed>` for a read that threw; one `  slot=<row>,* absent` row when the instance has no such array and `  slot=<row>,* empty` when it has none in it), read only through `variable_instance_get`, `array_length`, `array_get` and `variable_struct_get` and scaled to the window as a row's `win=` is; which array is the drawn bar and whether `navBbox` is the point to click are `slotRule`'s to confirm (`docs/skill-actions-research.md`).
    - A `UI_Inventory_Grid_obj` row is followed by one `  cell=<x>,<y> grid=<instance id> fp=<nodeFingerprint|none> o=none` row per occupied node of its `nodeGrid` (an array of rows of cells; a node struct carries `nodeStartX`, `nodeStartY`, `nodeLocked`, `nodeIsPermanent` and `nodeFingerprint` and no count, so `o` is always `none` - `cellRule`, live 2 P2-5), walked row by row, read only through `variable_instance_exists`/`get`, `array_length`, `array_get` and `variable_struct_exists`/`get`; an item covering several cells prints one row per cell. Cell rows do not count toward the 200-row cap; a grid with more than 200 occupied nodes prints the first 200 and its own row carries `cellcap=1` before `text=`. The hub matches a cell by `fp=` (`itemRule: fingerprint`). With no window open only the HUD belt's `PotionGrid` grid exists, so no bag cell is listed then.
    - Two `win=` limitations, both why every stash and bag tab switch goes by name: a child of a scrolled container reports its own `win=`, not the clipped one - the stash tab strip's rows do not land where the listing says (live 1 P0-5); and a bag sub-tab row's (`UI_Button_Inventory_Tab_Small_obj`) listed `win=` lands on the page tab above it (live 2 P2-4; the operator's empirical offset under 1920x1080 is a session note, never a route).
    - `win` is the instance's GUI position scaled by `window_get_width`/`window_get_height` over `display_get_gui_width`/`display_get_gui_height` and rounded - measured (with `menuprobe`, before this command existed) to map `Play local` to client (336, 534) windowed and (448, 712) fullscreen; `gui`/`bbox`/`view` print one decimal.
    - A failed read prints `<read-failed>` in that field rather than stopping the listing, and no double is formatted with a bare `%f` (Known Limitations item 10).
    - `menulayout <ObjectName>` lists that one object in the same format.
    - Nothing is hooked, performed, called, created, destroyed or written, and nothing of it is on the per-frame path.
    - A player build older than the command answers `command unavailable in player build: menulayout`.
    - First run against the game in phase 0, 2026-09-21, with the dev build: `Play local` was listed at `win=336,534`, and clicks at the listed `Play local` and slot-1 points both worked.
    - The player build's first live run is the hub's L-2 gate.

  - `menuprobe list <Obj>` / `event <Obj> <nth> <type> <number> [Obj2] confirm` / `script <Script> <Obj> <nth> [args ...] confirm` (**research build only**, not in `kPlayerCommands`, dispatched from `HandleMenuProbeCommand`): the character-select instrument; see `ForgePact/docs/character-select-research.md`.
    - `list` is read-only and needs no token: one line per live instance of that object with `nth`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `visible`, `sprite_index`, `image_index` and whichever of `text`, `label`, `action`, `script`, `selected` the instance actually carries, capped at 64, then a count.
    - It is also the **enumeration control** for the other two: a `list` that finds nothing at the main menu means the event and script candidates were *not measured*, not that they failed.

    - The control has to be this same command over an object the session has just seen live (`menuprobe list Menu_Controller_obj`, `Profile_Manager_obj` as the fallback): both listings empty measures the instrument rather than the button.
    - The reason is *not* that `citrace dumpobj` reaches an instance by a different path - reviewed 2026-09-21, `CiDumpNamedObject`, `MpResolve` and `MpList` run the same `asset_get_index` / `instance_number` / `instance_find` / `HhResolveInstance` sequence and differ only in how they read an instance once resolved.
    - The reason is that `list` exercises the same *read* path (`variable_instance_get`) the other two subcommands depend on.
    - `event` performs exactly one `event_perform` (or `event_perform_object` when an `<Obj2>` is given) on the chosen instance with it as both `self` and `other`; `script` makes exactly one `CallGameScriptEx` of `gml_Script_<Script>` the same way, numeric arguments as reals, `true`/`false` as bools, anything else as a string.
    - Both refuse with a usage line unless the last token is the literal word `confirm` (the `citrace` precedent: a half-written `cmd.txt` fails closed instead of firing), and both print the object, `nth`, instance `id`, position and the room index **before and after** the call, plus the result or the exception - so "refused", "ran and changed nothing" and "faulted" stay three distinguishable outcomes rather than one.
    - A `performed -> bool:true` proves the builtin ran, never that the event did anything.
    - Every instance is reached by name (`asset_get_index`, `instance_number`, `instance_find`, `HhResolveInstance`), no loop encloses either call and nothing is hooked.
    - Like every ForgePact command these run inside `PollCommands()`, which `FrameCallback` calls every 30 frames once `g_Setup` is set - which is exactly what makes calling `CallBuiltinEx`/`CallGameScriptEx` from them safe, the runtime being between frames and owned by that thread.
    - What the contract test pins is the narrower claim: nothing `menuprobe` adds sits *in* the per-frame path, so nothing of it runs unasked.
    - Expect faults from `script`: every cold call shape measured 2026-09-11 faulted and the process survived each one - what was never tried is a UI-action script with a real button as `self`, which is the only reason the subcommand exists.
