40. **Remove owned relics answers `GetRelicQuest`, the relic pick's own draw-again check, and reads the relic tab (ForgePact #125, hub #324, 2.1.0, 2026-09-30):**
    - **What was wrong.** 2.0.1 wrote each maxed relic's `droprate.base` to 1e18 around `DropRelic` and restored it after; its `holding back N of M` line proved only that the write landed. A static reading of the Sep-17 build (hub `docs/models/relic-pick-spec.md`) shows no relic pick reads that field: `DropRelic` draws `irandom(155)` and draws again while `GetRelicQuest` answers true (true for the quest relics 141..155 only), then may copy an equipped relic below level 10 in place of the pick. `EnemyKillSatanicZoneRelic` and `...Feast` run the same draw and never pass through `DropRelic`. The scan also missed the relic tab. So the reported relic (140, equipped at 10/10) dropped at its vanilla rate, 1 in 141 relic drops.
    - **What it does now.** `FrameCallback` installs `Hook_GetRelicQuest` once a player exists, and only a native detour counts: YYC calls the script directly, and a direct-call scan of the build found exactly three callers, the three relic routines. The hook asks the game first. For a relic the player owns at 10/10 it answers true while another relic is left (`RelicFilterMod::QuestAnswer`, `AnyRelicLeft`, the game's own answer per id probed once), so the game's loop draws again and the other relics keep equal odds; with every droppable relic maxed it stands down, since the loop would otherwise never end. The maxed set is scanned at most once per frame (`MaxedForFrame`) and includes the relic tab through the SDK's `ScanRelicTab` (`Controller_obj.inventoryData[key].inventoryRelicGrid`, key 1 online or the player row offline, the rule the game's own `PickupRelic` uses). AFK FARM's reward scope gets the game's answer untouched. `Hook_DropRelic` is only `dropmult relic`'s now, and no filter code writes the drop table.
    - **Tests:** hub `tests/test_relic_pick_model.py` (baseline, target, stand-down, and lever parity with this module's source), `tests/test_cpp_sdk.py` (`TestRelicTab`), `tests/test_relic_identification.py` (`TestSaveRelicTab`); here `tests/test_relic_filter_behavior.py` and `tests/test_relic_filter_contract.py` (`TestRelicFilterLever`).
    - **Live 1 (2026-09-30, dev build `D7C1815E...`, character Suh; hub `hs-game-sdk/curated/relic_pick_measurements.json`):**
      - **Setup.** Suh wore 68, 140, 15 and 29 at 10/10 and 109 at 2; the relic tab held 92 and 128 at 10/10.
      - **Hook.** `relicfilter: hook installed -> ON (GetRelicQuest, native detour)`.
      - **Arm scan.** `scan found 6 maxed relics (ids 15,29,68,92,128,140)`. The relic tab line read `nodes=100 ... relic=100 ... maxed=92@10,128@10 stopped=none`, equal to the save.
      - **Filter off.** 8 of 150 built relics were maxed.
      - **Filter on.** 0 of 150 were maxed, with 10 skips logged.
      - **Every droppable id but 7 and 109 test-maxed.** Only 7 and 109 came out, ten each.
      - **Quest relics.** No quest relic came out in 320 drops.
      - **The tab route's shape was measured in this session.** Two dev builds failed before it: the route first stopped at `inventoryData`, then read no fingerprints. So the SDK reads index `key - 1` and a node's `nodeFingerprint`.
      - **Restored.** ForgePact 2.0.0's DLL and the saves were restored or verified afterwards.
      - Capture: workorder `forgepact-125-relic-reroll-live-1.md`, 6/6 checks passed.

41. **Skill Haste and All Skills in `statadd` (ForgePact #114, hub #337, 2.1.0, 2026-09-30):**
    - **What it is.** Stat Forge's last two boosts, ported: `statadd` is now a three-entry additive table in `StatsManager.hpp` (`castrate`, `skillhaste`, `allskills`), each adding its bonus to element 0 of its `Stat*` script's array on a copy, after the game's calculation. The panel shows them in Modifiers → Offense (`PERCENT_STATS` rows: Skill Haste 0-200 step 5, All Skills 0-100 step 1, both off by default; All Skills reads `+N`, not `+N%`).
    - **The game side** (hub `docs/models/skill-stat-spec.md`, `RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS` § 7.5): `ReturnSpecificStat` dispatches stat 103 to `StatSpellHaste` and stat 2 to `StatAllSkills`, their only caller. `Controller_obj`'s Step lowers a skill cooldown's time left by `(1 + haste × 0.005) × deltaSpd` each step, so a cooldown lasts base / (1 + haste/200).
    - **Why the Skill Haste slider stops at 200, not Stat Forge's 500.** Live 1 measured that the game counts at most 200: totals of 240 and 340 ended Blade Barrier's cooldown in exactly as many steps as 200 did.
    - **Why only the native route arms.** YYC calls both scripts directly, so a table-only hook would log `HOOK INSTALLED` and add nothing; the install is refused with a line naming the route instead (the same rule as the relic filter's `GetRelicQuest`).
    - **The first-call line** (both builds) is how a player build shows the hook fired, since `BP_DIAG_INCREMENT` compiles away under `FORGEPACT_RELEASE`: `statadd StatSpellHaste: first boosted call 40 -> 140`.
    - **Tests:** hub `tests/test_skill_stat_model.py` (baseline, target, the cap, lever parity with this module's source, and `MeasuredTests` against `hs-game-sdk/curated/skill_stat_measurements.json`); here `tests/test_stat_add_behavior.py` + `tests/stat_add_harness.cpp` and `tests/test_stat_add_contract.py`, and the derived behaviour oracle's `NATIVE_SLIDERS`.
    - **Live 1 (2026-09-30, dev build `2311E933...`, character Suh, a Samurai with 40 Skill Haste from gear, in town):**
      - **Hooks.** `HOOK INSTALLED on StatSpellHaste` and `on StatAllSkills`, no TABLE-ONLY line; `statadd list` read `hook=native` for both.
      - **Method.** Blade Barrier (137, 8 s cooldown) cast from code with `tgprobe cast 137`; its cooldown counted as the Skill Haste reads the hook saw while it ran (the hook installed as a pass-through first, so the no-bonus runs count). One read per step, 60 a second, and none while no cooldown ran.
      - **Skill Haste.** First-call lines `40 -> 140` and `40 -> 340`. Steps: 392 and 397 with no bonus, 280 (+100), 265 (+120), 238 (+160, total 200), 238 (+200), 238 (+300).
      - **Interrupted.** At 23:57 another tool closed the game through AFK FARM's `game_session.py close` (a clean exit) and relaunched it for its own work, so the All Skills and save checks ran in a second session (below).
      - **Found on the way.** `ReturnTalentLevel` has no direct caller in this build, and calling it by name with only an id raises "I32 argument is undefined" (`skillprobe state`'s level lines); the game carried on.
    - **Live 1, session 2 (2026-10-01, dev build `42FD7566...`, the same character):**
      - **All Skills.** For Honor (142, one point) cast from code at 0 and at +19. First-call line `statadd StatAllSkills: first boosted call 28 -> 47`. Its buff (type 42) read `buffValue=[137.8,72.5,0]` at 0 and `[228,120,0]` at +19 (`skillprobe state bind=id:<buff>.buffValue`): the level times [4.75, 2.5], at 29 (1 point + 28 from gear) and 48.

42. **Headhunter and Tyrant's Crown join the game's own Angelic list for the length of each roll, only while their switch is on (ForgePact #74, hub #364, 2.2.0, 2026-10-02, owner-directed):**
    - **What a player gets.** Before (2.1.0) both items dropped only from the **Angelic / Unholy Drops** slider's own die, whatever their switches said (item 21). Now the slider never drops them: it builds only the game's real Angelic/Unholy uniques (49 read live on 2026-09-23; 47 candidates, 11 rejected in the first #74 Live 1, 2026-10-02). While the panel switch **Mods → Items → Headhunter** or **Mods → Items → Tyrant's Crown** is on, the item is one more entry in the list the game's own Angelic roll (the "Angelic item drop chance" effect of a Blood Pact or dungeon modifier) picks from: the game's picker and die decide, and on a hit that falls to it the game itself builds and places that item, one item per hit, in place of what the roll would otherwise have dropped, never beside it. The item's rarity is its stand-in's (below). ForgePact adds no die of its own and does not change the game's chance, its list between rolls or any unique's rate. Both switches off (the default) means no entry is ever added, neither item drops and the game's roll is untouched; forging an item turns its mechanic on, never this drop.
    - **The mechanism (static reading, hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 13.4).** `DropItemAngelicChance` re-picks a random entry `[type, sub, b]` of a list held by the first `Controller_obj` instance (object index 984) until the unique it names through `GetUniqueRepoStruct` passes the hidden-flag and rarity 7/10 filters, rolls a uniform integer against that definition's rate and hits when it is below the chance. Only on a hit does it call `CreateDefaultParams(sub, b, 1.0)` and then, by a direct call, the routine hooked as `LootGroundCreate`, which reaches `CreateItemNew`. Neither `CreateDefaultParams` nor the placement chain (`LootGroundCreate`, `CreateLootInFreePos`, `LootGroundInit`) reads the unique repository, and the item's `type` comes from the list entry, not from the parameters. The same list is read by merchants, shrines, crafting and other drop routines, which is why the added entries exist only for the length of one roll. The first #74 design's probe asked the global scope and `Loot_Manager_obj` for `lootListUnique`: measured on other scopes than the list's, so neither answer is about the list.
    - **The list's layout (static reading, replan 2, 2026-10-02; name and outer length confirmed by Live 1).** The list is not one flat array. `Controller_obj.lootListUnique` is an array of six elements (outer length measured by Live 1), of which the roll uses the sixth as a `ds_list`; Live 2 measured all six as `ref` `ds_list`s of triples (`[5] kind=ref ds_list=yes:380 triples=380/380`; the others 50, 61, 79, 152 and 221 entries), and what elements 0-4 mean is not established. The roll reads that sixth element by the constant index 5: `ds_list_size` on it, `ds_list_find_value` at a random index up to that size, then `is_array` on the value, re-drawing until it holds, and the value's elements 0, 1 and 2 are the `[type, sub, b]` handed to `GetUniqueRepoStruct`. The name comes from the record the runtime keeps beside the roll's variable slot (the first reading's four slot-name scripts searched stores and tables and found 0 hits), the three builtins from the records beside their pointer globals. **Not established:** what the other five elements mean (the sub-list's size is measured: 380 in Live 2, the same after a zone change and at the end of the session), and whether the random index can equal the size (the `is_array` re-draw would absorb it). `lootListNormal` (outer length 5) is not read by this roll. Hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 13.4 and the curated record's `list_layout` hold the same. ForgePact therefore resolves the list by a name and an index, `Controller_obj.<kAngelicListVar>[kAngelicListIndex]` with `kAngelicListIndex` 5 (the research build's `angelicprobe inject at <k>` moves it), requires the element to be a live `ds_list` of at least `kSigListMinSize` (10) entries, each an array of three numbers, counts `n` over that sub-list only, and pushes onto, reads back and cuts that `ds_list`, never the outer array. The live-list gate (`SigListHandle`) decides on the value as read, with no allow-list of handle kinds: it first refuses, before any conversion, a value of a kind that can never be a handle (array, string, struct, undefined or null, the named predicate `SigNeverAHandle`) as `never a handle`, because converting one is, by source reading, the runner's own REAL conversion, which raises a runner error a C++ catch cannot take back. That it raises is **measured** for an array (`report#2`, `REAL argument incorrect type array`, Live 3's capture) and for undefined (`REAL argument incorrect type undefined`, ForgePact#144, hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 5.4); for a string, a struct and null it is a **source reading**, not a measurement, and their error text has not been captured. That the research scan's 18 array and string elements raised the 18 errors each scan added in Live 2 and Live 3 is an arithmetic fit on the measured counts. Live 4 cannot settle the strings' share of it: the gate now refuses strings before converting them, so Live 4 can show only that the total stops rising (ForgePact `docs/angelic-roll-hook-research.md` Session 6). **Measured (Live 4, 2026-10-02, research dll `4b5994c3…`, ForgePact `ed59983`):** it stops. With the 15 arrays and 3 strings refused as `never a handle` and none `id unreadable`, a lone `angelicprobe inject auto` and then `angelicprobe list` left the YYError total at 1 (the launch's one report, raised in the menus before any command) where each scan had added 18 on the earlier builds, and the scan still accepted `lootListUnique[5]` (a ref, 380 entries). So the scan's conversions are measured as the cause of the rise; the strings' share of it is still the fit. Then `ToDouble` only refuses a value that is unreadable (the conversion throws), non-finite or negative, and then `ds_exists` is asked of the value itself with 2, `ds_type_list`. A real and a ref, and every kind the predicate does not name, go on to those steps, so a live handle is never refused by its kind; the kind is named in every refusal. Each refusal names its step (`... is not an array`, `has <L> elements, none at [<i>]`, `[<i>] array_get threw`, `[<i>] is not a ds_list (kind=<kind>, <step>)`, `[<i>] has <s> entries, fewer than <min>`, `[<i>] entry <k> is not three numbers`), where `<kind>` is `real`, `int32`, `int64`, `bool`, `string`, `struct`, `array`, `ptr`, `undefined`, `null` or `ref` (else `kind<N>`) and `<step>` is `never a handle`, `id unreadable`, `id non-finite`, `id <value>`, `ds_exists threw` or `ds_exists false`. The held read-back compares two reads by handle value, whatever kind each arrived as, and the dump's `ds_list=` uses the same gate.
    - **The table and the stand-in.** `kSignatureItems[]` in `ModuleMain.cpp` holds the mod items, one row each: display name, panel switch, the item's own `{t, a, b}` (Headhunter `8 / 777002 / 2`, Tyrant's Crown `0 / 777001 / 7`) and a **stand-in**, a real Angelic unique of the same `type` taken from `kAngelicBases` by name and resolved against the validated pool after `BuildAngelicPool`. Headhunter's stand-in is **Liquor Holster** `{8, 0, 51}` (the owner's choice in #74). Tyrant's Crown's is, until the owner names one, the validated helmet (`type` 0) with the lowest `droprate.base`, chosen when the pool is built and named in the switch-on log line. The stand-in gives the entry a definition the picker's filters accept and the stand-in's own drop rate, so the item's rarity is the stand-in's: that is what "Liquor Holster's share" means now. Miner's Helmet has no panel switch and is not in the table; adding it later is one row. A pool build that comes back empty (the game's unique data not loaded yet, as when the panel applies a switch at the main menu) is not kept: `BuildAngelicPool` logs its `angelic pool: 0 candidates` line once and is tried again by the next roll (with the roll's scope lowered, so none of the build's own script calls is taken for the roll's read or a hit) or switch-on, at most every 5 s, until a build finds candidates, which is kept for the session (PR review, 2026-10-03; before, the first empty build was kept and both stand-ins stayed unresolved, so neither switch could push, all session; `test_angelic_hit_behavior.py`'s `test_pool_retry`).
    - **The scoped push and remove, and the held read-back.** Inside `HookAngelicChance`, with at least one switch on and the list resolved, ForgePact remembers the sub-list's size (`ds_list_size`), pushes each enabled item's stand-in entry `[t, 0, b]` onto that `ds_list` (`ds_list_add`) before the first original call (exactly one per item in the player build, where `g_SigCopies` is the constant 1; the research build's `angelicprobe inject copies <k>` pushes k) and removes them after the last (ForgePact's own extra rolls included), under a scope guard so a throw removes them too. Right after the push comes the **held read-back** (`SignatureHeldReadBack`, both builds): the outer variable is read again by name off the first `Controller_obj` instance, a fresh `variable_instance_get` and never the handle just pushed onto, its element at the same index must be the same `ds_list` id, and the sub-list's size must be the old size plus the push and its tail must hold the pushed triples (`SignatureTailHolds`, over `ds_list_size` and `ds_list_find_value`). When it does not (another id, not a list, or a short tail), the entries come off the id pushed onto, one `inject: push not visible through Controller_obj.<name> ...` line is logged once per change, the roll is counted in `anomalies=` (and the research build's `heldMiss=`), and that roll carries nothing, so no hit in it is attributed; `injected=` counts only pushes the read-back confirmed. The read-back is light (the length and the pushed tail, never the full shape walk): it catches a copy, but it cannot show that the roll reads that variable, which is Live 1's `reach`. The removal checks the same tail, every copy included, and removes the entries only when the tail still holds exactly what it pushed (`ds_list_delete` of the last entry once per pushed entry, then the size must be the old size again); otherwise it leaves the list as found, logs one `inject: list changed during the roll, left as found` line and counts an anomaly. Between rolls the list is the game's own, byte for byte, so nothing is saved, the other readers never see the entries, and switching off needs no cleanup.
    - **Typing the hit (replan 1).** A third hook, `Hook_GetUniqueRepoStruct`, installed by its SDK name (`HookOneScript(SdkShortScriptName(HeroSiege::Scripts::gml_Script_GetUniqueRepoStruct), ...)`) inside `InstallSignatureAngelicHooks` beside the other two, always calls through and, only while the roll is in progress, records the `(type, sub, b)` it was asked for (three numbers, else the record is cleared); `SignatureHitReset` clears the record before each original call. When `Hook_CreateDefaultParams` sees a hit it takes the latest record only when that record's sub and b are the call's own first two arguments, and the hit is then **typed** as that whole triple. A hit with no such record is **untyped**: never attributed, never rewritten, left to the game and counted in `untyped=`, and its `angelic hit:` line reads `picked untyped <sub>/<b>`. **Measured** (Session 1, 2026-09-23): `GetUniqueRepoStruct` is called inside the roll about eight times per roll and its own detour sees those calls. **Static reading:** that the latest read before `CreateDefaultParams` is the picked entry's (the roll's order pick -> read -> re-pick on the filters -> die -> parameters); **measured** for the game's own entries by Live 1's `typing` check (57 of 57 hits typed and agreeing with the built item's type, below), and **measured on pushed entries** by Live 2: with 200 copies of Liquor Holster's entry pushed per roll, 65 of 80 hits fell on a pushed entry and all 80 were typed and agreed (`typeAgree` 46 to 126, `typeDisagree=0`, `untyped=0`), and the session ended at `typeAgree=211`, `typeDisagree=0` (hub `hs-game-sdk/curated/angelic_list_measurements.json`, `typing`). Because the identity is the whole triple, a unique of another type that shares the stand-in's sub and b (Liquor Holster's `0/51` is also Supreme Elemelon's, type 10) is never taken for the stand-in, so the first round's pool-based refusal of such a stand-in is gone. In the research build, `angelicprobe on`'s `unique-repo` row and this hook never both detour the script: whichever comes second refuses and says so (the typing hook as `detect=GetUniqueRepoStruct:held-by-angelicprobe`, which keeps the gate off; the row as `blocked: the #74 typing hook (Hook_GetUniqueRepoStruct) already holds this script`).
    - **The coin, and the game building the item.** A typed hit whose whole triple `(type, sub, b)` is the stand-in of an item this roll pushed is a candidate. The picker cannot tell the added entries from the vanilla ones: m items sharing that stand-in with k copies each hold m·k of its n + m·k entries, `n` being how often the vanilla sub-list holds that same whole triple (counted when the list is resolved and whenever its size changes), so a uniform draw gives the hit to a mod item with probability m·k / (n + m·k), which is 1 / (n + 1) in the player build: the stand-in keeps its own share and the mod item gets one entry's. On the mod item's hit it only attributes the hit (`g_SigHitItem`); `SignatureBeforeCreate`, in the `CreateItemNew` hook's pre-call slot, then writes `a`, `b`, `c` 0 and `j` 0 onto the item's `itemDefinitionStruct` (a missing field is created), reads them back, and on a refusal puts the record back, logs it, counts `refused=` and latches the item off for the session. The game's `LootGroundCreate` -> `CreateItemNew` then builds the Heavy Belt or Great Helm with seed `a`, and the Custom Forge hook recognises it by the selector `{t, a, b, c, j}` exactly as it recognises a `sigdrop` item. `SpawnSignatureItem` is not on this path; it stays for `sigdrop` and the research `replace` mode. Each hit logs one `angelic hit:` line naming the typed entry (`picked <type>/<sub>/<b>`, or `picked untyped <sub>/<b>`) and ending `-> vanilla` (with the stand-in's odds when it was a candidate, or `(untyped: ...)`) or `-> <item> (stand-in <name>, <m·k> in <n+m·k>) built by the game`.
    - **Detection (kept from the first #74 design, plus the typing hook).** `InstallSignatureAngelicHooks()` installs four hooks by name, each through `HookOneScript` so a first install gets the native detour that sees the roll's direct calls: `Hook_CreateDefaultParams` (`HookOneScript("CreateDefaultParams", ...)`, measured detourable in the #64 session), `HookAngelicChance` on `DropItemAngelicChance` when `g_OrigAngChance` is still null (the same install `raredrop angelic` and `angelicwatch` make), `Hook_GetUniqueRepoStruct` (above), and `Hook_CreateItemNew` on `CreateItemNew` when `g_Orig_CreateItemNew` is still null (the rewrite point; the Custom Forge usually holds that hook already from startup, and then its route is the one judged). A hit is visible and typable, and its record rewritable, only when all four are inline detours. `HookAngelicChance` holds a roll-in-progress state with a scope guard over the first original call and the extra-roll loop. The roll returns undefined on a hit exactly as on a miss, and `Hook_LootGroundCreate` stays a table-only `HookOneScriptTable` hook (`InstallItemInspectHooks` is pinned unchanged), blind to the roll's direct call, which is why the hit is seen at `CreateDefaultParams`. The research-only `ApRollChanceDepthScope` depth is separate and unchanged.
    - **Owner decisions in force** (2026-10-02): list injection first; the panel switch is the only gate; one hit is one item, in place of the roll's own drop (the first #74 design's drop beside the game's item, `SignatureShare` and `shareRolls=` are gone, replaced rather than kept); per-roll membership rather than persistent (a persistent entry would be seen by merchants, shrines and crafting and lost or duplicated by a rebuilt list); and the fallback **replace-at-hit** (the game places the stand-in, ForgePact destroys that one `Loot_Ground_obj` instance and spawns the item through `SpawnSignatureItem`) only if a live session shows that injection does not build the item. That fallback's risk would be a loot registry still listing the destroyed instance. Which helmet stands in for the crown is the owner's call (one table cell).
    - **The gate (owner, 2026-10-02: "Panel switch only").** `SignatureSwitchOn(0)` = `g_TyForced`, `SignatureSwitchOn(1)` = `g_HhForced`, both false unless the detection is all four inline detours (`g_SigDetectNative`: `CreateDefaultParams`, `DropItemAngelicChance`, `GetUniqueRepoStruct` and `CreateItemNew`; otherwise a hit would be invisible, untypable or unrewritable), and additionally the list must have resolved (`list=<name>[<index>]:<size>`); otherwise `gate=` stays off and the switch-on logs one refusal naming the variable and the step that failed. The player build resolves the list by the name in `kAngelicListVar` and the index `kAngelicListIndex` (5), checked as the layout bullet above says (a live `ds_list` of at least 10 entries, each an array of three numbers), and refuses with `list=missing` when that variable or its element fails the check. The constant is `lootListUnique`, the name Live 2's `reach` check passed on (it was empty, and the player build refused, until then). Those flags are what the panel's switch sets: an ON switch sends `tyrant force` / `headhunter force` at every game start and on the toggle, and `off` clears them. The console's `on` and the auto-arm from a forged item (`HeadhunterAutoArm()`, `TyrantAutoArm()`) set only `g_HhEnabled` / `g_TyEnabled`, the mechanic, so forging an item never turns its drop on. `tyrant status` / `headhunter status` print the gate as `angelicDrops=on|refused|not-resolved|no-detection|off`. The hooks are installed only from the `headhunter force` / `tyrant force` paths and the research build's `angelicprobe` levers, never from `EnableHeadhunter()`, the auto-arm, `InstallHook` or `ModuleInitialize`, so a session whose switches are off installs none of the four hooks; switching off installs nothing new and the hooks pass straight through. Nothing new runs in `FrameCallback`.

43. **Mining Ore Extra Rolls re-runs the game's own dig completion, so what it repeats and what it cannot give are the game's (issue #36, `miningrolls`, off by default, notes 2.2.0, 2026-09-28; verified in play on the shipped build 2026-10-02):**
    - **Repeats per roll, by design.** Only mining XP, character and guild XP, quest progress and the floating text are silenced during an extra run (§ "Mining Ore Amount and the Miner's Helmet"), and of those only character and guild XP were measured once per dig. No dig was seen calling `MiningAdd`, `CombatText` or `update_quest`, so mining XP, quest progress and the floating text may still repeat per roll: not established, and not measured on 2026-10-02 because the test character's mining level was at the 5000 cap (the owner chose to ship without it). The dig sound (`PlaySound3D`), the `Mining_Effect_obj` hit effect, and any other floating text the completion draws other than through `CombatText` run once per roll; `NetworkSendClient` also runs per roll and does nothing offline.
    - **Bonus finds need the character's own stats.** An extra roll draws the dig's stat-gated bonus finds again (query ids 693-700), but a character whose stats are all 0 never passes one, however many rolls: the rolls then give only more ore. Which gear or talents raise those stats is not established (`docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 12).
    - **A node whose re-run does not pay is left depleted.** An extra run that pays no ore stops the loop, logs `miningrolls: extra roll paid nothing - stopped after <k> of <n> extra rolls` once, and the node's `hp` is forced to 0 whatever happened; that node's remaining rolls are lost. The completion did pay again in the same frame in every measured case (13 of 13 extra runs on 2026-09-28, 2 of 2 on 2026-10-02), so this is a guard, not an observed outcome; `ForgePact/docs/mining-ore-research.md` § "Extra rolls".
    - **The rolls refuse to arm if any of their seven detours is table-only** (the step/loot pair, the four pass-through detours, the shared `CombatText` one), and name it in `miningrolls: unavailable - <script> came up table-only`. For example, after `citrace nativetrace` detoured `update_quest` directly in a research session. The multiplier is not affected.
    - **Tests:** `tests/test_mining_ore_behavior.py` + `mining_ore_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_release_hook_contract.py`, the hub's `tests/test_mining_reward_model.py`.
44. **"Sleep loot your filter hides" (`hiddenloot`, #95 part 2b, off by default, 2026-09-28) deactivates instances the game created, and has three consequences it accepts rather than fixes:**
    - **Loosening the filter does not reveal slept items.** A deactivated instance is not drawn whatever its verdict, and whether the game's loot-filter menu re-evaluation reaches one is not established (`docs/hidden-loot-research.md` § "Not established"). The player holds the show key, or switches the mod off; a woken item keeps the hidden verdict it had until the filter is next applied.
    - **Only the verdict at drop time counts.** An item a later, stricter filter hides stays awake: the mod judges an item once, at the end of the frame it dropped in (or in the switch-on walk).
    - **The pet ignores slept items**, exactly as it ignored hidden ones (it collects only filter-visible items, `docs/pet-loot-stuck-research.md` § "The scan"). While the key is held, the shown items become targets it can pick up.
    - **The runtime-suspension rule (AGENTS.md § "Don't Suspend the Game's Own Runtime") was assessed and the risk accepted.** The mod does not take the loop away from the game: it deactivates only instances the game itself has chosen to hide, as far sleep does with props, and only at the end of a frame, never inside the game's own drop call (whose caller may still address the new instance). Its failure mode is "a hidden item stays hidden" or "stays hidden and awake", not a soft-lock; the switch reverses it in play (`hiddenloot 0` wakes everything it slept, with the game's hidden verdict in place), and the room's end cleans up either way. That last point is measured for awake hidden loot (809 of 809 Clean Up runs, Live 1 of `forgepact-issue-95`), for sleeping props (far sleep), and for sleeping loot (1,495 of 1,495 Clean Up runs and no Destroy, `zone-end-asleep` of Live 2 of `forgepact-issue-95-mod`, 2026-09-28). `ForgePact/docs/menu-pause-plan.md` §0 was read for this assessment.
    - **The default show key is Left Alt (VK 164, owner, 2026-09-28).** A lone Alt press can put a Win32 window into its menu mode, a modal loop that could stall the game's frames or eat the next keystroke. For this game's window it did not: Live 2 of `forgepact-issue-95-mod` (2026-09-28, `alt-no-menu`, pass) pressed and released Left Alt once by injected input, and the game stayed in front, answered `ping`, and showed no system menu and no game menu. That is one injected press on one machine; a player whose window does go into menu mode picks another key in **Show hidden loot while held**. Whether the game binds Left Alt to anything itself is not established. Generic Alt (18), Right Alt (165) and F10 are not offered, and the mouse buttons 1 and 2 are refused.
    - **Measured live** (Live 2 of `forgepact-issue-95-mod`, 2026-09-28, research DLL `52414e0f...f968`, the hook before its in-call reduction; the reduced hook is harness-verified 2026-10-02 and was measured live in Live 3 of `forgepact-issue-95-mod`, 2026-10-02, research DLL `1d828170...45f1`, `inits=473 slept=462 errors=0`, argument 0 carrying the item in every call): the hook sees the game's own drop calls (`route=both`, `inits=531 slept=522`), the key under injected input shows and re-hides (522 woken and slept again; the game's refresh did not re-hide them), and sleeping loot is cleaned up at the zone's end; see "Hidden loot sleep (`hiddenloot`)" below. **Not observed live:** `LootGroundDrop`, an item picked up while shown, and the table-only fallback pass, which are harness-verified only; which woken items were off screen while the key was held (the `invisible=` half of `hold-shows`, confounded by the on-screen gate).
    - **Tests:** `tests/test_hidden_loot_behavior.py` + `hidden_loot_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_hidden_loot_mod_contract.py`, `tests/test_hidden_loot_panel_contract.py`.

45. **The Bosses control raises a boss through the shared `EnemyRaritySettings` hook; health, damage, XP and the drop rank are measured on one Ancient boss, the rest is not observed (issue #44, `bossrarity`, Mods → Gameplay, off by default, notes 2.2.0; live 2026-10-02: Live procedures 1 rerun and 1b on the research build, Live procedure 2 on the release build `b235c9fd…5c81`):**
    - **The hook is the shared one.** The raise is a branch of `Hook_EnemyRaritySettings`, installed by `InstallTyrantHook()` (by name through `HookOneScript`, both routes), the hook the Monster Rarity sliders and Tyrant's Crown already use; the research build installs it at startup, the player build on the first `bossrarity rare|ancient`. `bossrarity off` leaves it installed. A `failed` install refuses the mode: `bossrarity rare|ancient` then answers `bossrarity: refused <mode> hook=failed (...; unchanged: <mode>)` and leaves the mode where it was (`StoresMode` in `BossRarityMod.hpp`, as Tyrant's Crown refuses in that case), since the install is attempted once per session and a stored mode would report itself armed while raising nothing. A `table-only` install keeps the mode, and its status line's `hook=table-only` says that bosses compiled GML creates through direct calls are not raised. The panel's `/api/set` still answers ok and keeps the saved value on a refusal; only the plugin's line shows it.
    - **Bosses the game already rolled above rank 1 are left alone.** Only a boss at `enemyRarity` exactly 1 is raised; one the game made champion, rare or ancient keeps its rarity and counts as `notRank1`. How often a boss arrives above 1 on its own is not known.
    - **Enemy-born phase objects are left alone.** A boss another monster created (Odin's second phase, Architect clones, the player clone) is enemy-born and stays at the game's own rarity, the sliders' rule, so a split child is never raised again and again.
    - **Uber Luna is never tested from outside.** Killing it from outside closed the game on 2026-09-26 (`docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 13.1), so no live step spawns or kills it; whether the raise behaves on it is not observed.
    - **What the raise changes, measured on one boss (route `boss-rarity: beyond-hp`, `boss-drops: raised`).** On the research build a Karp King to Rare and to Ancient and Damien, Uber Damien and Uber Anubis to Ancient read back at the hook's exit at the rank written with the top-up's affixes. On an Ancient Karp King the game built from that rank: health ×5.65 (Live 1 rerun) and ×4.73 (Live 1b) its rank-1 read, each with its own affixes and neither with a health control, so whether a boss follows the ordinary rank table on health is not established; damage ×2.10 (×1.90 on the ordinary rank table, so 10.4% above it) and XP on kill ×6.25 (the table's exact row), the records the protected-store keys in `damage` and `killExperience` name (not those variables' values, which are the keys), read through `bossprobe`'s proven getter and counted only because an ordinary monster raised the same way moved by the table's ratios on the same read (`rank-damage-control`, `rank-xp-control`); and `DropItem`'s rank argument 4 instead of 1 at its traced death. **Not observed:** an ancient look (name bar and body unchanged in one shot), more drops (10 against 12 `itemdrops.jsonl` lines, one kill each), boss gems, runes or parts, and every dimension at Rare. The README, the 2.2.0 notes and the Gameplay card claim only the measured values; `test_boss_rarity_panel.py` keeps the card free of damage, drops and XP while the research doc's `## Live procedure 1` section does not mark them measured (Live 1b's are in its own section). The affix top-up (up to 2 at Rare, 3 at Ancient) is the sliders' own floor, not a count the game chose for a boss.
    - **The release build is confirmed through the panel, not on a boss (Live procedure 2, 2026-10-02).** With `b235c9fd…5c81` installed and the panel served from this branch, the saved `forgepact.json` carried no `boss_rarity` and the startup list no `bossrarity` line; `POST /api/set {"key":"boss_rarity","value":"ancient"}` answered ok and `bossrarity status` read `ancient ... hook=ok`, `HOOK INSTALLED on EnemyRaritySettings` with no `TABLE-ONLY` line in `out.txt`; an explicit `off` POST read `bossrarity: off`. `shipped-boss` was not run (the owner's choice), so the raise itself is measured on the research build only.
    - **The counters say what was attempted.** `raised` counts writes that did not throw; nothing reads `enemyRarity` back. `seen` counts only bosses judged while the mode is on, so `seen=0 hook=ok` does not tell "no boss came through" from "the hook never ran".
    - **Tyrant's Crown reads the raised rarity.** The crown's block runs after the raise in the same hook, so with the crown on a boss raised to Rare can also get the crown's extra affix (our code; not observed live).
    - **The first Live 1 aborted after its control (2026-10-02); the rerun ran the same day on the detached research build.** The DLL hash, the load marker and the control (Karp King `ENTRY`/`EXIT` at `enemyRarity=1`) passed; then the game froze in a console flood of the runner's `YYError` text from `timer_system_update`, a different object id on each line (owner-observed; nothing in `out.txt`). The hero stood in a Hell zone at level 243 whose load had already stalled 50.5 s. What left those timers without an owner is not established: neither the raw spawn nor the zone's own population is measured as the cause. The rerun used the research build that detaches from the console (the #58 entry above), a zone confirmed by screenshot and a liveness check after every spawn, and did not freeze (19 of its 26 checks passed, none failed). Record: `ForgePact/docs/boss-rarity-research.md`, `## Live procedure 1`.
    - **A `cb` spawn raised a runner error in the enemy-born guard; fixed, reach into the player build not established.** In the Live 1 rerun YYToolkit full report #2 (`REAL argument incorrect type undefined`) carried plugin frames that a relinked map of the session's own objects resolves to `HookICD` → `EnemyBornScope` → `CallerObjectIndex`, under the research `cb` command. `CallerObjectIndex` converted the creating `self`'s `object_index` with `RValue::ToDouble()`, the runner's `REAL_RValue`, which on an undefined value raises the runner's error instead of throwing, so its `catch (...)` never saw it; `cb` creates with a `self` that is not a game instance. `CallerObjectIndex`, `InstanceIdOf` and the research-only `TyInstName` now check the kind first (`IsNumericInstanceRead`: REAL, INT32, INT64, REF) and read anything else as unknown (-1, `?`). The guard is in both builds, but whether any game path creates a monster from a `self` without `object_index` is not established, so the release notes do not claim a player fix. The traced Karp King deaths that dropped nothing are not the trace's doing (`tests/test_droptrace_contract.py`); what the game decided there is not established, and Live procedure 1b pairs every kill with `dropstats` (research doc § "The plugin's runner error and the traced kills").
    - Research: [`ForgePact/docs/boss-rarity-research.md`](../../../ForgePact/docs/boss-rarity-research.md). **Tests:** `tests/test_boss_rarity_behavior.py` + `boss_rarity_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_caller_kind_behavior.py` + `caller_kind_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_droptrace_contract.py`, `tests/test_bossprobe_object_contract.py`, `tests/test_boss_rarity_contract.py`, `tests/test_boss_rarity_panel.py`, `tests/test_rarity_boss_exclusion_contract.py`.
46. **Pet collects relics calls the game's loot pickup the way the companion does, built from a static reading and confirmed live: the collect and the skip on the research build (Live 1), the switch through the panel on the player build (Live 2) (issue #124, hub #378, `petrelic`, off by default, notes 2.2.0, 2026-10-02):**
    - **What ships.** A Quality of Life switch, `mod_pet_relic_pickup` / `petrelic 1`, separate from the Pet Quest Collector. While the pet is out it walks to the nearest relic on screen whose owned copy is not 10/10 and calls `PickupLoot` by name with the companion's own shape (`self` the ground relic, `other` the pet, `argc` 5; § 2, `petrelic`), one at a time, through the quest collector's selector (hold-back, cursor) and its travel helper. Only route A (`PickupLoot`) is in the player build; route B (`PickupRelic` directly), `stat`, `census`, `route` and `trace` are research-only (`tests/test_pet_relic_collector_contract.py` pins it). There is no capacity check: the relic bag has one slot per relic (owner, #124).
    - **Why a relic needs its own route.** A dropped relic is a `Loot_Ground_obj` (class 16), not a `Quest_Object_Parent_obj`, so the quest collector's `m_Questpickup` call does not apply; the game's own pet never takes it (its type filter, hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 10.6); and `LootGroundRelicStep` is the relic's floating animation, not a walk-over pickup (§ 10.7 there). Static reading.
    - **The skip rule, and where the maxed set comes from.** A relic is maxed by the owned copy's level (relic tab or equipped), never the dropped relic's (it always drops at 1). The tick reads the local player's owned relic levels through `hs-game-sdk` (`HeroSiege::Player::GetOwnedRelicLevels`), not `RelicFilterMod::GetPlayerMaxedRelics`, which answers nothing while the relic filter is off (planner default, reversible at one call site), and adds `relicfilter testmaxed`'s ids so Live 1 can prove the skip without a real 10/10 relic. A maxed relic is left out before the selector sees it, so a screen of maxed relics leaves the pet idle by construction (`target/only_maxed_picks_none`). The set is re-read at most once per 60 ticks and straight after a collect that returned true. Those scans are struct walks, and one that stops early returns a smaller, plausible set rather than failing - and the relic-tab 10/10 copy it might leave out is exactly the one whose pickup consumes the relic for nothing. So a read counts only when both scan reports (`EquippedSlotScanReport`, `RelicTabScanReport`) say `stopped == nullptr`: the tick keeps the last complete set, targets nothing until it has one, and the collect refuses (`maxed-scan-incomplete(<scan>:<stage>)`) when its own read just before the call is not complete.
    - **What `petrelic 0` reports.** One line, `PetRelicCollectorMod::StatLine()`: `collected=`, the skips (`skipped(maxed)=`, `skipped(not relic)=`, `skipped(gate)=`, `itemActive missing=`), `refused=` with its last reason (no pet, no player, no item, no itemInstance, call threw, no callable, returned false, `maxed-scan-incomplete(<scan>:<stage>)`), the true returns that left the relic on the ground, the plugin's own destroys, `target lost=`, `travel timeouts=`, `held back=`, `maxed scans=`, `maxed ids=`, `route=` and `phase=`. The research doc's § "What `petrelic 0` and `petrelic stat` count" says what each field is evidence of. The first eight refusals also log one line each, with what the call was supplied.
    - **Who destroys the relic.** By the static reading neither `PickupLoot` nor `PickupRelic` destroys the ground instance; each of the game's callers does, after a true return. So the plugin destroys the relic itself, only after a true return (`test_destroy_only_inside_the_true_return_branch`), and only once it has seen the effect: the owned level of that relic exactly one higher than just before the call, or the id newly owned, read whole. A true return with no raise seen, or an after-read that stopped early, destroys nothing and holds the relic back rather than retrying it (a raise the read missed would be raised again); a false return or a throw destroys nothing.
    - **The relic-tab 10/10 outcome is not established.** By the reading, `PickupRelic` returns false for an equipped copy at 10/10 (the relic stays: the "cannot be picked up" the owner reports) but true, with nothing raised, for a relic-tab copy at 10/10, so a caller would consume the ground relic for nothing. Not established live, and recorded as a game fact rather than acted on. The pet cannot reach that branch while its owned-level read is complete, it refuses to collect when the read is not, and a true return that raised nothing destroys nothing.
    - **Live status, 2026-10-02, Sorak (slot 14): the collect confirmed on the research build, the switch confirmed on the player build.** **Live 1** (research build, sha256 `a591ff14a32da319ab3bd4764cb2a423ce1d31d1f40778063ba4caca88239fd6`, capture `forgepact-124-pet-relics-live-1.md`, 14/14 checks pass): `petrelic trace` on the player's own click pickup confirmed the call shape (`self` the ground item, `argc` 5, the ground relic still there after a true return); the pet collected 31 relics through route A (`pickup-route: pickuploot`, so route B stays research-only), raising relics 73, 106 and 131 from 9 to 10; `ReadGroundRelic` read 42 of 42 relics on screen; 12 relics owned at 10/10 and the two `relicfilter testmaxed` ids were never taken; and a screen holding only maxed relics left the pet idle (`phase=idle`, no travel timeout). **Live 2** (player build `BloodPactPlugin_ship.dll`, sha256 `1db502603bd93432ed5badb027489113c102b0c50a1ec7a03c1054e74c762ee8`, from ForgePact `fc797dc`, capture `forgepact-124-pet-relics-live-2.md`, 7/7 checks pass: `dll-hash`, `marker`, `control`, `panel-on`, `research-only`, `panel-off`, `panel-launch`): confirmed through the panel on the player build. The Mods-tab request (`/api/set mod_pet_relic_pickup`, sent headless, not clicked) turned it on (`petrelic -> ON (...)` within 3 s) and off (`petrelic -> OFF` plus the stat line); `petrelic stat` answered `command unavailable in player build` and left the switch on; and a panel restarted with the switch saved on sent `petrelic 1`. Not observed live: a relic the game itself dropped being collected (Live 1's relics were all placed by `forcerelic`), a pet collect on the player build (Live 2 had no relic on the ground; the pickup code is the same in both builds), and `petrelic 1` sent on a game relaunch rather than a panel restart. Details are in the research doc's `## Live 1 results` and `## Live 2 results`.
    - **Tests:** `tests/test_pet_relic_collector_behavior.py` + `pet_relic_collector_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_pet_relic_collector_contract.py`, `tests/test_pet_relic_panel_contract.py`, and the quest collector's own suites, which pin the travel code it now shares (`tests/test_pet_quest_collector_behavior.py`, `tests/test_pet_quest_collector_contract.py`).
47. **Jump through scenery (`jumpscenery`, #16 phase 2, off by default, 2026-10-03) answers the player's own collision queries during a jump, and only where its landing guard allows; what it cannot see, it leaves to the game:**
    - **The reach is learned only from a clear jump.** The landing is take-off + reach × direction, and the reach comes from a recent jump of at least 32 px in which the mod answered nothing and no take-off query was blocked; nothing seeds it. So the first jump after loading a character, and the first after a large Jump Power change, behaves as vanilla (`refused-no-reach=`) or checks the landing at the old reach. A reach that is too short lands inside the obstacle and is refused (safe); one that is too long can grant a landing beyond a free point. The 16 px band around the landing and the next clean jump bound that.
    - **Curated J7 and J8 stay refused.** In phase 1's Live 1 a jump aimed to land inside a horse carriage (curated J7, Live 1 run J4) and one aimed north into a building or prop area (curated J8, Live 1 run J5) did not start even with every hooked query answered. The game refuses them by a route these five builtins do not cover (`InstancePlaceTallest`, an `instance_place` from another `self`, or something unhooked: not established), and the mod does not answer it (no script rows, no `place_free`, no tiles). Mod live 1 (2026-10-03) repeated the carriage case through the mod (curated J14): the jump was granted and 1152 queries answered, and the player did not move. Curated ids are those in `hs-game-sdk/curated/jump_measurements.json`; the research doc's Live 1 run labels (J1 to J5) are not curated ids.
    - **Co-op is not measured.** Only the local player counts as `self`; every other player's queries get the game's answers.
    - **`skillsLeap` may be shared with a Leap skill: not observed** (Sorak had none on the bar). If the game's own Leap skill runs it too, that skill's take-off would open the window as well; the decision and the landing guard are the same.
    - **The pass set.** The `Collision_Parent_obj` family, which includes `Wall_Parent_obj` (map edges: the landing check's `place_meeting` refuses a landing inside a wall, harness-verified; the room check does not guard the walkable map's edge, since `Town_01_rm`'s room extends past it, so what happens there is not observed), `Lever_Parent_obj`, `Quest_NPC_Parent_obj` and `Chaos_Tower_Collision_obj`, but not `Gate_Parent_obj` or `Lock_obj` and their descendants (the owner, 2026-10-03). Whether a gate or a lock blocks a jump through these builtins at all is **not observed live**; the harness pins the exclusion, and no live check is planned.
    - **Where the window opens.** Mod live 1 (2026-10-03) measured that the take-off walk runs inside `skillsLeap`'s first call: `walk-in-window=` rose by one on each of three jumps with the mod on and `walk-before-open=` stayed 0. If a game patch moves the walk, read the two again: `walk-before-open=` above 0 and `walk-in-window=` at 0 on a crossing jump means the take-off walk ran before the window opened, which needs a different opener (and its own measurement first), not a fix in the adapter. Both at 0 means no walk circle reached the mod as family, which is a failed family test and not a result. `before-open=` alone is contaminated by walking and standing checks.
    - **Neither guard has been seen working live.** At Live 1's horse carriage the mod granted the jump and the player did not move at all (`refused-landing=0`, `landed-inside=0`), so the landing guard ran and let it through; the point it checked was not recorded, so whether that point lay inside the carriage is not established, and the guard has not been seen refusing a landing; the owner reads it as the game validating the landing zone itself, which is not a measured mechanism. The room guard was not reached either: `Town_01_rm`'s room is 2800 × 2400, larger than its walkable map, so `playerwarp` points within 100 px of a room edge were out of bounds and no edge jump was made. Both guards stay in, harness-verified only. **What happens at the walkable map's edge, and whether the game ejects a landing inside a prop, are not observed.**
    - **A crossing jump ends shorter than the learned reach.** In Mod live 1 the jump across Live 1's prop moved 125 px against a learned `reach=178` (an open-ground jump of about 175 px); why is not established. So the point the landing guard checks (take-off + reach × direction) was not where that jump ended: the player stopped about 50 px before it, in the open.
    - **Tests:** `tests/test_jump_scenery_mod_behavior.py` + `jump_scenery_mod_harness.cpp`, `tests/test_jump_scenery_mod_contract.py`, `tests/test_jump_scenery_panel_contract.py`.

48. **Satanic Zone control picks the zone the game treats as satanic through the game's own protected value (`satzone`, ForgePact #157, off by default, notes 2.2.0, 2026-10-04):**
    - **What ships.** Two World-tab switches and one command, both builds. **Keep the zone you are in satanic** (`satzone follow 1`) pins the act zone the player is in and keeps it pinned as they move; **Every zone counts as satanic** (`satzone everywhere 1`) forces `LoadSatanicZone`'s answer true for every call without touching which zone is resolved; the command adds `satzone pin here|<index>` (one exact zone), `satzone off` (release pin and follow) and `satzone stat`. With both switches off nothing changes. While on, each switch is an ordinary entry in the panel's Enabled mods list with a Turn off button (`BOOLEAN_MODS` in `panel/src/enabled-mods.js`; the pools' all-on-by-default exclusion, item 27, does not cover off-by-default switches). The panel rows, the command, the entries and the resolver pair are pinned by `tests/test_satanic_zone_control.py`; the command is also named in the two exact `kPlayerCommands` pins (`test_forge_hash_contract.py`, `test_toggle_skill_contract.py`).
    - **How it touches the game.** The key is read from `Controller_obj.satanicZone` at runtime; the value is read and written through the game's own `GPV`/`SPV` scripts with the local player as `self` (the shape the 2026-10-03 probes used) - no address, no struct layout, and never a `variable_instance_set` on the key. The pin re-asserts on the satmods 15-frame poll because the game re-rolls its own value. Towns and sub-areas are refused as targets by room-name shape (`Act_NN_MM`; the tracker's `IsActZoneRoomName` precedent). `everywhere` installs its hook from the frame tick once a player exists (char select must not get hooks - the `restartanytime` rule), retried every few hundred frames.
    - **The player-resolution trap, hit and fixed live.** `instance_find(Player_obj)` hands back a `VALUE_REF` on this runner (the 2026-09-10 measurement behind `HhResolveLocalPlayer`); the first version's `ToDouble()` + `GetInstanceObject` path resolved no player in the frame tick (live: `refused=30`, "player instance unreadable") while the command path worked. Both reads and writes now go through `HhResolveLocalPlayer` + `HhResolveInstance`, and the contract test pins the pair and the absence of `GetInstanceObject`.
    - **Live 2026-10-04 (test character, town, dev build).** `satzone pin 44` wrote the value and it held (`pcall GPV 162966` 85 -> 44; `writes=1`, no refusals); `satzone pin here` and `satzone pin 235` refused the town as "not an act zone"; `satzone follow 1` skipped the town (no writes); `satzone everywhere 1` installed the `LoadSatanicZone` hook from the frame tick (`satmods status`: hook=on, `calls=450`), and `everywhere 0` / `off` released with zero refusals.
    - **Live 4 (2026-10-04): the in-zone effect is confirmed, and the map marker is a separate layer.** `LoadSatanicZone(room)` answers "is the player in that act-zone room?" (true for `Act_01_01`'s room while standing in it, false for another room and for the town), and the game calls it every frame with the store's value, so `pin`/`follow` make the game's own state true exactly while the player stands in the named room. Entering `Act_01_01` with `satzone pin 1` already set added five `Draw_Player_Buff_obj` buffs to the player (the same slots read empty with the pin off) and the player saw the satanic buffs and debuffs on the buff bar; releasing the pin mid-zone did not remove objects already applied. Still unwatched: a relic drop in a satanic zone, and the `everywhere` switch's own effect in play (only the forced answer, 10k+ calls, was measured). The world map's red marker is the game's own per-node display layer (`UI_Map_Zone_Button_obj.isSatanic` with its image/timer fields, set when the game itself resolves a zone): pinning the store, the game's own re-rolls, `everywhere` and invoking every node's own `m_RefreshNode` (63 nodes, through the `citrace invoke obj` probe) all left it unchanged, so the control feature does not drive it. The research record is `docs/satanic-zone-mods-research.md` § "Live 3", § "Live 4" and § "The shipped control".
49. **Projectile amount, projectile speed and AoE size sliders: the research phase, with all three routes proven live on a White Mage (issue #160, hub #408, `projprobe`, research build only, 2026-10-04):**
    - **Nothing player-visible ships yet.** No panel row, no `statadd` entry, no release notes. This phase leaves `docs/skill-sliders-research.md` (the static reading, the candidate table and `## Live 1`, the three sessions' results), the research build's `projprobe` (§ Command Reference) and the hub's model (`docs/models/skill-sliders-spec.md`, `hs_game_sdk.skill_sliders_model`, checked against `hs-game-sdk/curated/skill_sliders_measurements.json`). The sliders are the next workorder, and start from the routes below. Route tokens: `amount-route: proven`, `speed-route: proven`, `aoe-route: proven`.
    - **Projectile amount: the two shared helpers.** `ReturnExtraSpellProjectiles` returns a spell skill's adjusted total (stat 394 as a percent, floored, plus stat 311), and `ReturnExtraProjectilesRanged` only an extra count its caller adds (stat 239 plus chance-based bonuses from 451/452 and 240); 44 and 19 direct call sites in the `Talents<Class>` scripts (static reading). Measured (Live 2, Shadow Bolt): the helper's return is the number of bolts; `projprobe amount 2` turned a return of 1 into 3 and one bolt into three. `ReturnExtraProjectilesRanged` was not observed (no White Mage call).
    - **AoE size: the `statadd` route.** Stat 554 goes through `ReturnSpecificStat` to `StatAOESkillSize`, whose only direct caller found is the dispatcher, the `StatSpellHaste` shape item 41 already detours natively. Measured (Live 3, Soul Spurn): `projprobe aoe 50` on element 0 made stat 554 read 50 inside `LoadAllModifiers`, put 0.5 in the skill object's `projEffect[1086]`, and grew its `image_xscale`/`image_yscale` from 7.5 to 8.0. The element reaches a White Mage object through `SetAllModifiersNew` and is applied by the object's parent event (static reading). **The Healing Zone is the outlier**: its branch makes no `SetAllModifiersNew` call and it clamps its own scale to 1.5, so it did not grow at +50 (Live 2 and Live 3).
    - **Projectile speed: stats 74 and 75 under `LoadAllModifiers`.** They have no `Stat*` script and no dispatcher case; `LoadAllModifiers` reads both (0 on Sorak, Live 1 `ids`). Measured (Live 2, Shadow Bolt, the stat form `speed stat <id> add <bonus>`): stat 75 is a percent of the object's `deltaSpeed` (+0.5 gave ×1.005, +50 gave ×1.5), stat 74 a flat 5/12 of `deltaSpeed` per point (+0.208333, +20.833333), and the `speed` built-in followed `deltaSpeed` × `deltaTimer` on every read. Not observed: the order the two combine in, which one the tooltip's "Projectile Speed" is, and the instance form (`speed <mult>` after `LoadProjectileSettings`), which only `Projectile_Player_obj` (the basic attack's object) reaches; no basic attack was seen. Which form may ship is the owner's call in the next workorder.
    - **The routes reach more than the player's own casts** (measured): `Mercenary_obj` calls `LoadAllModifiers` while it fights (beside `LoadProjectileSettings` calls on `Projectile_Player_obj`), the double-cast proc `Universal_Double_Cast_obj` calls `ReturnExtraSpellProjectiles`, `StatAOESkillSize` and `LoadAllModifiers` itself, and many casts carry a second, base-6 `ReturnExtraSpellProjectiles` call that the amount lever also raised (6 -> 8). A slider has to scope itself or accept that. Summons and NPCs that call `LoadAllModifiers` were not observed.
    - **Tests:** `tests/test_skill_sliders_probe_contract.py` (the probe's rows, flags, arming and the research-build gate), `tests/test_release_hook_contract.py` (nothing of it reaches the player build), and in the hub `tests/test_skill_sliders_model.py` (`MeasuredTests` reads the curated rows).

---

## Maintenance Triggers

- **A new test module:** it must pass alone as well as in the serial run, because `tools/run_tests_parallel.py` runs each module in its own process alongside others. Import what it needs itself (put `src/` on `sys.path` before loading `src/forgepact.py`), bind port 0, and write only under a directory unique to it (`tempfile`, or its own `build/<name>`). Check with `py -3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p <module>.py` from `ForgePact/`. A module that starts a browser declares `PARALLEL_GROUP`; one that measures timing declares `PARALLEL_EXCLUSIVE = True`, so it runs alone at the end. A new panel browser suite gets a module of its own (not a method in an existing one, since the runner parallelises by module), imports `_missing` and `_npm` from `tests/panel_browser.py`, and declares `PARALLEL_GROUP = "panel-browser"`; `tests/test_run_tests_parallel.py` fails if it does not.
- **Game Executable Updates:** When a new Season 10 patch releases, verify that spawner object names, GML function names, and `LoadDrops` drop family indices remain valid. The player build contains **no raw game addresses** to re-verify (Known Limitations item 11) — everything resolves by name or off a YYToolkit struct — so a new build should surface as named lookups failing, not as a crash. Player-build closure names (`anon@N@...`) come from `HeroSiege::Scripts` constants, so regenerating hs-game-sdk after a patch that moves one surfaces it as a compile error and a failing `test_player_build_closure_names_all_match_the_sdk`, instead of a silent runtime name-lookup failure. The dev-only `kCiCallMethodFnRva` does need re-verifying before anyone runs `citrace collect confirm native`; `citrace dispatchdump` / `citrace symdump` in the research build are the tools for re-locating it.
  - **Player-build hooks that rest on a static reading of the game: `DropItemAngelicChance`, `CreateDefaultParams` and `GetUniqueRepoStruct` (#74, Known Limitations item 42).** The signature drop counts a `CreateDefaultParams` call during `DropItemAngelicChance` as a hit, because the roll calls it only on a hit. After a patch, re-read the roll locally (hub `docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md` § 13.4) and confirm `CreateDefaultParams` is still called only on the hit path and nowhere else inside the roll; otherwise misses would be rewritten into signature items. The typing hook on `GetUniqueRepoStruct` rests on the roll's read order (pick an entry, read its definition, re-pick on the filters, roll the die, then build the parameters), so the latest definition read before `CreateDefaultParams` is the picked entry's: a static reading, measured on the game's own entries in Live 1 of `forgepact-74-angelic-list-injection` (2026-10-02, `untyped=0`, `typeAgree=57`, `typeDisagree=0`). After a patch, re-read that order too; live, `untyped=` on `sigdrop status` must stay 0 over hits (an untyped hit means no read inside the roll agreed with the hit's sub and b, and the item is never attributed), and the research build's `typeDisagree=` must stay 0 against `typeAgree=`. A patch can also move what the injection resolves by name: the list's variable on `Controller_obj` (`kAngelicListVar`, recorded as `list_variable` in hub `hs-game-sdk/curated/angelic_list_measurements.json`; a renamed or reshaped variable makes the player build refuse with `list=missing`), the sub-list index the roll reads (`kAngelicListIndex`, 5, the constant index of the roll's read, recorded as the curated record's `list_layout.index`; a moved index leaves the player build pushing onto an element the roll no longer draws from, which only `reach` would show, so re-read it and re-run `angelicprobe list dump` after a patch), the sub-list being a `ds_list`, the list entry's `[type, sub, b]` shape, the stand-ins' repository indices (`kAngelicBases`, validated by the pool), and the item record's field names `a`, `b`, `c`, `j` at CreateItemNew's entry (`itemDefinitionStruct`; the rewrite creates a missing one and refuses only when a value does not read back). `angelicprobe list` and `angelicprobe inject status` plus `sigdrop status`'s `gameRolls=`/`gameHits=`/`injected=`/`ourHits=`/`untyped=`/`built=`/`anomalies=`/`list=` are the live check, read only once the same line's `cdpCalls=` is above zero and `detect=` reads `detoured` (all four detours, on `CreateDefaultParams`, `DropItemAngelicChance`, `GetUniqueRepoStruct` and `CreateItemNew`, survived the patch).
  - **Closure names move with every game patch.** The player build now spells them through `HeroSiege::Scripts` constants (above), so a regeneration surfaces as a compile error rather than a silent hook. Done (2026-09-18): player names now match hub `4539e68`'s SDK, regenerated for the current game build (`data.win` `07D864C9…`) - e.g. `GenerateItemHash@anon@4645` is `GenerateItemHash@anon@4791` there - on ForgePact branch `fix/closure-names-current-game`, merged into `feat/prospect-window-research`. The 25 research-only `citrace` closure literals moved with them; the seven `Quest_Object_Parent_obj` and ten `Profile_Manager_obj` closures were mapped by ordinal position within their Create event (equal counts, monotone offset growth), so the `m_Quest*` method-name labels the research code attaches carry over by inference only, not observed on the current build. `test_citrace_closure_hooks_cover_every_sdk_closure_of_their_objects` now fails the next regeneration loudly (naming which closures exist and which are hooked) instead of drifting silently. ForgePact's release CI (`forgepact-release.yml`) builds against hub `main`'s SDK, so hub #74 (the SDK regeneration) and this fix must land together - merging one without the other breaks the release build one way or the other. `prospectprobe`'s table already uses SDK constants.
  - **Pet collects relics reads the ground item by name.** A game update that renames the ground item's object (`Loot_Ground_obj`), its `itemInstance` variable, the class or definition variables inside it (`itemType`, `itemDefinitionStruct`), or the pickup scripts (`PickupLoot`, `PickupRelic`) breaks `petrelic`: the SDK's `ReadGroundRelic` then refuses every ground item and the pet picks nothing (`skipped(not relic)=` rises in `petrelic 0`), or the call reports `no callable`. The research build's `petrelic census` shows which: its `read stages:` summary names the stage the read stopped at, and it prints the variable names of the first ground item and of its `itemInstance` struct. Fix the names in `hs-game-sdk` (`player.hpp`), not in the plugin.
- **YYToolkit Header / Binary Sync:** Any rebuild of `YYToolkit.dll` requires recompiling `BloodPactPlugin` against matching headers in `plugin_build\include\` to prevent vtable mismatch crashes. Because the plugin now reads `CScriptRef` directly (under `/DYYTK_DEFINE_INTERNAL=1`), a header update also has to keep those layouts truthful — the headers' own `static_assert(sizeof(YYObjectBase) == 0x88)` is the compile-time check, and `petquest stat`'s `REFUSED (structural)` line is the runtime one.
  - The hub's `third_party/yytoolkit/` series is pinned to the same upstream commit as these headers (`5a95e46`, tag v4.0.1) and touches none of the plugin-facing files (`YYToolkit/source/YYTK/Shared/`, `ExamplePlugin/`), so a DLL built from it is meant to keep working with a plugin compiled against the unmodified pinned headers. One behaviour does change for a plugin: `CreateCallback(EVENT_OBJECT_CALL)` returns `AURIE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of succeeding with a callback that never fires. `BloodPactPlugin` registers `EVENT_FRAME` only, so this is not expected to affect it — observed live on 2026-09-19: `BloodPactPlugin` v1.4.4 loaded and initialized against a build of this series, `EVENT_FRAME` kept firing (it drives the plugin's IPC poll), and zero `REFUSED EVENT_OBJECT_CALL` lines were logged in that idle session (see `third_party/yytoolkit/README.md`, "Second launch results (2026-09-19, plugin loaded)").
- **Dependency Upgrades (YYToolkit):** A change to the distributed YYToolkit — a new upstream version, a fix, a build flag — is made in the hub, not here: move the pin in `third_party/yytoolkit/upstream.json`, refresh or add patches under `third_party/yytoolkit/patches/` (each with its mandatory header), and rebuild with `tools/build_yytoolkit.py`; that directory's README has the procedure and the launch gate. What has to survive an upstream bump is the whole of `patches/series`, not "the disk cache and the `ExecuteIt` change" — that two-item list described the old notice, and the old notice did not describe the binary. Never rebuild `YYToolkit.dll` from `yytoolkit-modified/` or from any tree that is not the pinned commit plus the series.
- **Moving the `YYToolkit.dll` pin (merged, PR 53; not yet shipped in a release):** PR 53 (1) repointed `tools/toolchain-pins.json` at the hub release asset for a launch-gated build of the hub series, with its SHA-256 and the hub commit as provenance — the pin count stays eleven; (2) rewrote `yytoolkit-modified/NOTICE.md` to point at the hub directory and deleted the two whole-file copies in the same commit; (3) corrected `CREDITS.md` and `README.md`, which used to say "one modified source file"; (4) ships the notice and `YYToolkit-BUILD-INFO.json` with the binary — `build_release.py` now copies both into `modfiles/` alongside `README.md`, `CREDITS.md` and `LICENSE`; (5) carries `release-notes-v1.4.4.md`, naming what was and was not launch-tested rather than claiming a settled fix; (6) deleted `ensure_ri_cache`'s hand-measured RVA table from `src/forgepact.py`, which patch `0001` made unnecessary. It merged to `origin` after the launch gate carried a plugin-loaded row and the owner's confirmation, together with HS-Offline-Tracker's equivalent (PR 3) — see `third_party/yytoolkit/README.md`, "Where the binary is published". The hub release its pin names exists and is published (not marked `--latest`), and the asset URL it points at resolves. **What remains is the owner's decision to tag and release ForgePact 1.4.4** (and HS-Offline-Tracker 0.1.3 alongside it, since both install to `mods/aurie/YYToolkit.dll` with overwrite semantics) — that is a separate, still-outstanding step from either the merge or the published library release.
- **A control added to, or changed on, the panel:** the markup goes in the tab it belongs to, `panel/src/tabs/*.svelte` (shared logic in the plain-JS modules under `panel/src/`), and never back into `src/forgepact.py`, which only decides what the control's `/api/set` sends. Never re-record the behaviour oracle: `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle.json` is the legacy page's recording and the only proof the port kept every old control's behaviour (its `oracle:record` npm script passes `--legacy`; this checkout no longer embeds the pre-port page, and an older ref's page is served only through the sandbox server's `--src`, which records a supplement, never the legacy file). Instead add the new or changed control to the derivation in `panel/tests/oracle-derive.mjs`, re-run `npm run oracle:derive` in `panel/`, and commit the regenerated `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle-derived.json` with the change, never hand-editing any oracle JSON file - Representative Change Workflow step 3 says the same, and `npm run oracle:replay` fails its coverage check on an enumerated control that no oracle file lists. A control a pre-port legacy page had but the legacy recording predates (the Gems of Incarnation controls, from origin/main at `f1e2f57`) is covered by the recorded supplement `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle-gems.json` (`npm run oracle:record:gems -- --src <dir> --source-rev <sha>`) and by `npm run e2e:gems`; a change to those controls is re-checked against both. When a supplement-recorded control moves to another tab or card, the move goes into `SUPPLEMENT_RELOCATION` in `panel/tests/lib/oracle-relocate.mjs` (navigation steps only; it refuses a step that sent anything), then `npm run oracle:derive`, never into the recording and never by re-recording it from this tree. A key a later origin/main adds to `KEYS` is covered by a supplement recorded from main's page (as `panel/tests/behaviour-oracle-primeevil.json` is, through `record --only primeevil` and replay's `--key-supplement`) plus an entry in `ADDED_KEYS` for `insertAddedKeys` in `panel/tests/lib/oracle-relocate.mjs`, the reset line the backend now adds to every full key reset the older recordings hold, never by editing a recording; `insertAddedKeys` throws on a recording that already sends the line. Rebuild with `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run build` before replaying or packaging, and write its contract test's page pins through `tests/panel_source.py` (`panel_source()` or `panel_file('<file>')`), not by reading a built file or `forgepact.py`. A visual change also needs a fresh screenshot baseline (`run screens`), compared deliberately rather than accepted. After any `panel/src` change, rebuild and run `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run e2e:perf`: it must stay `26/26`, and a check that fails on a noisy machine gets more `--runs`, never a looser budget. After a motion change (anything in `app.css` that transitions, `@starting-style`, `[data-instant]`, or the JS that sets it), also run `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run e2e:motion` and add a `motion-M<k>` check for a new motion (and after a change to the theme picker, the check marks, the gutters or anything else the finish review fixed, `npm --prefix ForgePact/panel run e2e:finish`, then update `panel/DESIGN.md`): motion uses the `--motion-*` tokens only, never runs on anything a poll repaints or on a keyboard action, and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` removes movement and scale while opacity and colour fades stay, as the export's `motion.notes` says (`amendments.ship`).
- **A Figma design export made or re-made (`panel/design/figma-export.json`):** give each `components[]` entry the `selector` the panel draws it as, and each `selectorTokens` entry that belongs to one its `component`, and make `node ForgePact/panel/tests/design-match.mjs --structure --export <export> --out <dir>` exit 0 an acceptance criterion of the export workorder itself, not of the restyle after it. In the UI redesign (2026-09-24..27) the export disagreed with the panel's page seven times (value strings, 68 texts, a bare `.val` matching outside its stepper, a font path, a baked-in version), each found only at restyle, at the cost of two restyle rounds, two Figma rounds and three replans (hub `docs/agents/workorder-calibration.md`, "Why the ForgePact UI redesign took 60 hours (2026-09-27)", added by hub PR #264 and measured from the redesign's transcripts and context Logs; the earlier "about 48 hours" in "Spending each check once" was read from plan-file dates). The committed export predates `component`, so its structure run reports `placement: no selectorTokens entry names a component` until the next export adds them.

## Miner's Helmet
